translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 276
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 276

sentences.zh: 【後唐紀五】 起強圉大淵獻七月，盡屠維赤奮若，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Tang Records 5] From the seventh month of the Qiangyu Dayuanxian cycle through the Tuyu Chifenruo cycle—in all, a little more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Tang Records 5] From the seventh month of the Qiangyu Dayuanxian year through the Tuyu Chifenruo year—a little more than two years in all.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝中之上天成二年（

translations.literal: Middle section of Emperor Mingzong the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Filially Pious—upper part, Tiancheng year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Filially Pious—middle section, upper part: Tiancheng year 2 (

sentences.zh: 丁亥，公元九二七年）

translations.literal: dinghai, CE 927)
translations.idiomatic: dinghai, 927 CE)

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以歸德節度使王晏球為北面副招討使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Gui De military governor Wang Yanqiu was made deputy northern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Yanqiu, military governor of Guide, was appointed deputy northern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，升夔州為寧江軍，以西方鄴為節度使。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Qizhou was elevated to Ningjiang Circuit, and Xi Fangye was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Qizhou was promoted to Ningjiang Circuit, with Xi Fangye as its military governor.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以與高季興夔、忠、萬三州為豆盧革、韋說之罪，皆賜死。

translations.literal: On guiyou, for the crime of ceding the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan to Gao Jixing, Dou Luge and Wei Shuo were both granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Dou Luge and Wei Shuo were both ordered to take their own lives, having been convicted of surrendering the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan to Gao Jixing.

sentences.zh: 流段凝於遼州，溫韜於德州，劉訓於濮州。

translations.literal: Duan Ning was exiled to Liaozhou, Wen Tao to Dezhou, and Liu Xun to Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ning was banished to Liaozhou, Wen Tao to Dezhou, and Liu Xun to Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 任圜請致仕居磁州，許之。

translations.literal: Ren Yuan requested to retire and live in Cizhou; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan asked to retire and reside in Cizhou; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 八月，己卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day jimao of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the new moon of jimao, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 冊禮使至長沙，楚王殷始建國，立宮殿，置百官，皆如天子，或微更其名：翰林學士曰文苑學士，知制誥曰知辭制，樞密院曰左右機要司，群下稱之曰殿下，令曰教。

translations.literal: The investiture envoy reached Changsha; King Yin of Chu first established a state, erected palaces, and installed the hundred officials—all like the Son of Heaven, though some titles were slightly altered: Hanlin academician was called Literary Garden academician, drafter of edicts was called drafter of proclamations, the Bureau of Military Affairs was called the Left and Right Secret Affairs Offices, subordinates addressed him as Your Highness, and orders were called teachings.
translations.idiomatic: When the investiture envoy reached Changsha, King Yin of Chu formally founded his state. He built palaces and appointed a full bureaucracy on the model of the imperial court, with only slight changes to some titles: Hanlin academicians became Literary Garden academicians, edict drafters became proclamation drafters, the Bureau of Military Affairs became the Left and Right Secret Affairs Offices, subjects addressed him as Your Highness, and his commands were styled teachings.

sentences.zh: 以姚彥章為左丞相，許德勳為右丞相，李鐸為司徒，崔穎為司空，拓跋恆為僕射，張彥瑤、張迎判機要司。

translations.literal: Yao Yanzhang was made left chief minister, Xu Dexun right chief minister, Li Duo Minister of Education, Cui Ying Minister of Works, Tuoba Heng Grand Counselor, and Zhang Yanyao and Zhang Ying were assigned to the Secret Affairs Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanzhang was appointed left chief minister, Xu Dexun right chief minister, Li Duo Minister of Education, Cui Ying Minister of Works, and Tuoba Heng Grand Counselor; Zhang Yanyao and Zhang Ying oversaw the Secret Affairs Offices.

sentences.zh: 然管內官屬皆稱攝，惟朗、桂節度使先除後請命。

translations.literal: Yet officials within his domain were all styled acting; only the military governors of Lang and Gui were appointed first and then submitted for imperial confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: Within his realm, however, all officials were designated acting appointees; only the military governors of Lang and Gui were installed first and sought imperial confirmation afterward.

sentences.zh: 恆本姓元，避殷父訊改焉。

translations.literal: Heng's original surname was Yuan; he changed it to avoid the taboo on Yin's father's name, Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Heng had originally borne the surname Yuan but changed it to avoid the taboo on King Yin's father's name, Xun.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝謂安重誨曰：「從榮左右有矯宣朕旨，令勿接儒生，恐弱人志氣者。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the emperor said to An Chonghui, "Around Congrong there are those who falsely proclaim my edict, ordering that Confucian scholars not be received, fearing they may weaken men's resolve.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the emperor told An Chonghui, "Some of those around Congrong have been forging my orders, telling people not to admit Confucian scholars for fear they might sap men's resolve.

sentences.zh: 朕以從榮年少臨大籓，故擇名儒使輔導之，今奸人所言乃如此！」

translations.literal: Because Congrong is young and presides over a great frontier command, I chose eminent Confucians to instruct and guide him—yet now the words of these villains are such as this!"
translations.idiomatic: I chose distinguished scholars to guide him because he is young and holds a major frontier post—yet this is what these schemers are saying!"

sentences.zh: 欲斬之；

translations.literal: He wished to execute them;
translations.idiomatic: He wanted them put to death;

sentences.zh: 重誨請嚴戒而已。

translations.literal: Chonghui asked only for strict admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui urged strict warnings instead.

sentences.zh: 北都留守李彥超請複姓符，從之。

translations.literal: Northern Capital garrison commander Li Yanchao requested to restore the surname Fu; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanchao, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, asked to resume the surname Fu; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以樞密使孔循兼東都留守。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Kong Xun was additionally made Eastern Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Kong Xun, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was also appointed garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 壬申，契丹來請修好，遣使報之。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Khitan came requesting renewed friendship; an envoy was dispatched in reply.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the Khitan sought to restore friendly relations; the court sent an envoy in response.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙酉，帝發洛陽，將如汴州；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, the emperor departed Luoyang, intending to go to Bianzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yiyou, the emperor left Luoyang, planning to travel to Bianzhou;

sentences.zh: 丁亥，至滎陽。

translations.literal: On dinghai, he reached Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he reached Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 民間訛言帝欲自擊吳，又雲欲制置東方諸侯。

translations.literal: Among the people false rumors spread that the emperor wished to attack Wu in person, and also that he intended to reorganize the eastern feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread among the people that the emperor meant to lead a personal campaign against Wu, and also that he planned to reorganize the eastern feudatories.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使、檢校侍中朱守殷疑懼，判官高密孫晟勸守殷反，守殷遂乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Xuanwu military governor and acting Palace Attendant Zhu Shouyin grew suspicious and afraid; his judge Sun Sheng of Gaomi urged Shouyin to rebel, and Shouyin thereupon manned the walls and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shouyin, military governor of Xuanwu and acting Palace Attendant, grew fearful. His aide Sun Sheng of Gaomi urged him to rebel, and Shouyin manned the walls in defiance.

sentences.zh: 帝遣宣徽使范延光往諭之，延光曰：「不早擊之，則汴城堅矣；

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Secretariat commissioner Fan Yanguang to instruct him; Yanguang said, "If we do not strike early, Bian City will be firmly held;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Fan Yanguang, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, to reason with him. Yanguang said, "If we do not attack soon, Bian will be firmly held;

sentences.zh: 願得五百騎與俱。」

translations.literal: I wish to have five hundred horsemen go with me."
translations.idiomatic: I ask for five hundred cavalry to go with me."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 延光暮發，未明行二百里，抵大梁城下，與汴人戰，汴人大驚。

translations.literal: Yanguang set out at dusk; before dawn he had marched two hundred li, reached beneath the walls of Daliang, fought the men of Bian, and the people of Bian were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang set out at dusk. Before dawn he had ridden two hundred li, reached the walls of Daliang, and clashed with the defenders, throwing the city into great alarm.

sentences.zh: 戊子，帝至京水，遣御營使石敬瑭將親兵倍道繼之。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the emperor reached Jingshui and dispatched Imperial Camp commissioner Shi Jingtang to lead the personal guard by forced marches in support.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the emperor reached Jingshui and sent Shi Jingtang, commissioner of the Imperial Camp, to hurry the personal guard forward in support.

sentences.zh: 或謂安重誨曰：「失職在外之人，乘賊未破，或能為患，不如除之。」

translations.literal: Someone said to An Chonghui, "A man who has lost office and remains outside—while the rebels are not yet broken, he might become a threat; better to eliminate him."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told An Chonghui, "A dismissed official still at large might cause trouble while the rebels remain unbeaten—it would be better to remove him."

sentences.zh: 重誨以為然，奏遣使賜任圜死。

translations.literal: Chonghui thought this correct and memorialized to send an envoy granting Ren Yuan death.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui agreed and memorialized that an envoy be sent to order Ren Yuan to die.

sentences.zh: 端明殿學士趙鳳哭胃重誨曰：「任圜義士，安肯為逆！

translations.literal: Duanming Hall academician Zhao Feng wept and rebuked Chonghui, saying, "Ren Yuan is a man of righteousness—how could he turn rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng, academician of the Duanming Hall, wept as he rebuked Chonghui: "Ren Yuan is a man of honor—how could he rebel!

sentences.zh: 公濫刑如此，何以贊國！」

translations.literal: You abuse punishments thus—how can you assist the state!"
translations.idiomatic: With such reckless executions, how can you serve the realm!"

sentences.zh: 使者至磁州，圜聚其族酣飲，然後死，神情不撓。

translations.literal: When the envoy reached Cizhou, Yuan gathered his clan for a hearty drink, then died, his expression unbent.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reached Cizhou, Yuan gathered his clan for a final feast, then accepted death without flinching.

sentences.zh: 己丑，帝至大梁，四面進攻，吏民縋城出降者甚眾。

translations.literal: On jichou, the emperor reached Daliang; attacks pressed from all four sides, and very many officials and commoners let themselves down by rope from the walls to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the emperor reached Daliang. As attacks closed in from every side, large numbers of officials and townspeople lowered themselves from the walls by rope to surrender.

sentences.zh: 守殷知事不濟，盡殺其族，引頸命左右斬之。

translations.literal: Shouyin knew affairs could not succeed, slaughtered his entire clan, stretched out his neck, and ordered those beside him to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that all was lost, Shouyin killed his entire clan, bared his neck, and told his attendants to strike off his head.

sentences.zh: 乘城者望見乘輿，相帥開門降。

translations.literal: Those on the walls saw the imperial carriage, led one another, and opened the gates to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders on the walls sighted the imperial carriage and opened the gates to surrender in succession.

sentences.zh: 孫晟奔吳，徐知誥客之。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng fled to Wu, and Xu Zhigao received him as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng fled to Wu, where Xu Zhigao entertained him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，詔免三司逋負近二百萬緡。

translations.literal: On wuxu, an edict remitted nearly two million strings in arrears owed to the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu an edict remitted nearly two million strings of debt owed to the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，吳大丞相、都督中外諸軍事、諸道都統、鎮海、寧國節度使兼中書令東海王徐溫卒。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Wu's Grand Chief Minister, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad, Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits, military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, and Concurrent Palace Secretariat Director, Prince of Donghai Xu Wen, died.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Xu Wen, Prince of the Eastern Sea—Wu grand chief minister, commander-in-chief of all military affairs at home and abroad, commander-in-chief of all circuits, and military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo—died.

sentences.zh: 初，溫子行軍司馬、忠義節度使、同平章事知詢以其兄知誥非徐氏子，數請代之執吳政，溫曰：「汝曹皆不如也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Wen's son, Acting Army Marshal, Zhongyi military governor, and Concurrent Associate Chief Minister Zhixun, because his elder brother Zhigao was not a son of the Xu clan, repeatedly asked to replace him in governing Wu affairs; Wen said, "You are all inferior to him."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wen's son Zhixun—acting army marshal, military governor of Zhongyi, and associate chief minister—had repeatedly asked to take over Wu government affairs, arguing that his elder brother Zhigao was not a Xu by blood. Wen replied, "None of you measures up to him."

sentences.zh: 嚴可求及行軍副使徐玠屢勸溫以知詢代知誥，溫以知誥孝謹，不忍也。

translations.literal: Yan Keqiu and Acting Army Deputy Commissioner Xu Jie repeatedly urged Wen to replace Zhigao with Zhixun; Wen, because Zhigao was filial and cautious, could not bear to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Keqiu and the acting army deputy commissioner Xu Jie repeatedly urged Wen to replace Zhigao with Zhixun, but Wen, finding Zhigao filial and prudent, could not bring himself to do it.

sentences.zh: 陳夫人曰：「知誥自我家貧賤時養之，奈何富貴而棄之！」

translations.literal: Lady Chen said, "Zhigao was raised by us from the time our family was poor and lowly—how can we abandon him once we are rich and noble!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen said, "We raised Zhigao when our family was poor—how can we cast him aside now that we are prosperous!"

sentences.zh: 可求等言之不已。

translations.literal: Keqiu and the others spoke without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu and the others would not let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 溫欲帥諸籓鎮入朝，勸吳王稱帝，將行，有疾，乃遣知詢奉表勸進，因留代知誥執政。

translations.literal: Wen wished to lead the various frontier commands to court to urge the King of Wu to take the imperial title; about to depart, he fell ill, and so dispatched Zhixun to present a memorial urging accession, remaining behind to replace Zhigao in administering government.
translations.idiomatic: Wen planned to lead the frontier commands to court to urge the King of Wu to assume the imperial title, but fell ill before he could depart. He sent Zhixun north with a memorial urging accession and kept him there to replace Zhigao in governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 知誥草表欲求洪州節度使，俟旦上之，是夕，溫凶問至，乃止。

translations.literal: Zhigao drafted a memorial requesting the military governorship of Hongzhou, intending to submit it at dawn; that evening news of Wen's death arrived, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao drafted a memorial asking for the military governorship of Hongzhou and planned to submit it at dawn, but that evening word of Wen's death arrived and he set the memorial aside.

sentences.zh: 知詢亟歸金陵。

translations.literal: Zhixun hastened back to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun hurried back to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 吳主贈溫齊王，謚曰忠武。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler posthumously enfeoffed Wen as Prince of Qi and gave the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu posthumously enfeoffed Wen as Prince of Qi with the posthumous title Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 山南西道節度使張筠久疾，將佐請見，不許。

translations.literal: Shannan West Circuit military governor Zhang Yun had long been ill; his generals and aides requested an audience and were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, had been ill for a long time. When his officers and staff asked to see him, they were refused.

sentences.zh: 副使苻彥琳等疑其已死，恐左右有奸謀，請權交符印；

translations.literal: Deputy commissioner Fu Yanlin and others suspected he was already dead, feared treachery among those close at hand, and requested temporary transfer of the tally and seal;
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioner Fu Yanlin and others suspected Yun was already dead and feared a plot among his attendants; they asked to take temporary custody of the command tally and seal;

sentences.zh: 筠怒，收彥琳及判官都指揮使下獄，誣以謀反。

translations.literal: Yun was enraged, seized Yanlin and the judge, the commander-in-chief of the capital guard, and imprisoned them, falsely charging rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yun flew into a rage, arrested Yanlin and the capital guard commander, who served as his judge, and imprisoned them on a trumped-up charge of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔取彥琳等詣闕，按之無狀，釋之；

translations.literal: an edict ordered Yanlin and the others brought to court; investigation found no basis, and they were released;
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Yanlin and the others brought to the capital. Investigation found no evidence of wrongdoing and they were released;

sentences.zh: 徙筠為西都留守。

translations.literal: Yun was transferred to Western Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was reassigned as garrison commander of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以保義節度使石敬瑭為宣武節度使，兼侍衛親軍馬步都指揮使。

translations.literal: On guimao, Baoyi military governor Shi Jingtang was made Xuanwu military governor and concurrently Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry and Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Shi Jingtang, military governor of Baoyi, was appointed military governor of Xuanwu and commander of the palace guard cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚戌，吳王即皇帝位，追尊孝武王曰武皇帝，景王曰景皇帝，宣王曰宣皇帝。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, the King of Wu assumed the imperial position, posthumously honoring the Filially Martial King as Emperor Martial, the Luminous King as Emperor Luminous, and the Accomplished King as Emperor Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengxu, the King of Wu took the throne. He posthumously honored the Filially Martial King as Emperor Martial, the Luminous King as Emperor Luminous, and the Accomplished King as Emperor Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 安重誨議伐吳，帝不從。

translations.literal: An Chonghui proposed attacking Wu; the emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui urged a campaign against Wu, but the emperor would not agree.

sentences.zh: 甲子，吳大赦，改元乾貞。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Qianzhen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Wu proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Qianzhen.

sentences.zh: 丙子，吳主尊太妃王氏曰皇太后，以徐知詢為諸道副都統、鎮海寧國節度使兼侍中，加徐知誥都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Wu ruler honored the Senior Consort, Lady Wang, as Empress Dowager, made Xu Zhixun Deputy Commander-in-Chief of All Circuits and military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo with concurrent Palace Attendant rank, and added to Xu Zhigao the title Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs at Home and Abroad.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the Wu emperor honored Senior Consort Lady Wang as empress dowager, appointed Xu Zhixun deputy commander-in-chief of all circuits and military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo with the rank of palace attendant, and added to Xu Zhigao the title commander-in-chief of all military affairs at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊寅朔，孟知祥發民丁二十萬修成都城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day wuyin of the month, Meng Zhixiang mobilized two hundred thousand corvée laborers to repair the walls of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the new moon of wuyin, Meng Zhixiang drafted two hundred thousand laborers to repair the walls of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 吳主立兄廬江公濛為常山王，弟鄱陽公澈為平原王，兄子南昌公珙為建安王。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler enfeoffed his elder brother, Duke of Lujiang Meng, as Prince of Changshan; his younger brother, Duke of Poyang Che, as Prince of Pingyuan; and his elder brother's son, Duke of Nanchang Gong, as Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu emperor enfeoffed his elder brother Meng, Duke of Lujiang, as Prince of Changshan; his younger brother Che, Duke of Poyang, as Prince of Pingyuan; and his nephew Gong, Duke of Nanchang, as Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 初，晉陽相者周玄豹嘗言帝貴不可言，帝即位，欲召詣闕。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Jin Yang diviner Zhou Xuanbao had once said the emperor's nobility was beyond words; after the emperor took the throne, he wished to summon him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Jin Yang diviner Zhou Xuanbao had foretold that the emperor's destiny was beyond ordinary description. After his accession, the emperor wished to summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳曰：「玄豹言陛下當為天子，今已驗矣，無所復詢。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng said, "Xuanbao said Your Majesty would become Son of Heaven—this is already verified; there is nothing further to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng said, "Xuanbao predicted that Your Majesty would become emperor, and that has already come true. There is nothing left to ask.

sentences.zh: 若置之京師，則輕躁狂險之人必輻輳其門，爭問吉凶。

translations.literal: If he is placed in the capital, then frivolous, reckless, and dangerous men will surely crowd his gate, competing to ask fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: If he is kept in the capital, reckless and unscrupulous men will flock to his door, all clamoring to learn their fortunes.

sentences.zh: 自古術士妄言，致人族滅者多矣，非所以靖國家也。」

translations.literal: Since antiquity, practitioners who speak rashly have caused many clans to be exterminated—this is not the means to bring peace to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Throughout history, fortune-tellers' reckless words have led to the destruction of many families. That is no way to secure the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝乃就除光祿卿致仕，厚賜金帛而已。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon appointed him Retired Grand Master for Splendid Happiness on the spot, with generous gifts of gold and silk only.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed him retired Grand Master for Splendid Happiness on the spot and rewarded him generously with gold and silk, but did not summon him.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人馬縞請用漢光武故事，七廟之外別立親廟；

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat drafter Ma Gao requested to follow the precedent of Emperor Guangwu of Han and establish separate ancestral temples for close kin outside the seven temples;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gao, a drafter in the Palace Secretariat, proposed following the precedent of Emperor Guangwu of Han by establishing separate ancestral temples for close kin outside the seven main temples;

sentences.zh: 中書門下奏請如漢孝德、孝仁皇例，稱皇不稱帝。

translations.literal: the Secretariat memorialized requesting that, following the examples of the Han Filially Virtuous and Filially Benevolent Emperors, they be styled huang and not di.
translations.idiomatic: the Secretariat memorialized that, following the Han examples of the Filially Virtuous and Filially Benevolent Emperors, they should be styled huang rather than di.

sentences.zh: 帝欲兼稱帝，群臣乃引德明、玄元、興聖皇帝例，皆立廟京師；

translations.literal: the emperor wished to use both titles di; the ministers then cited the precedents of Emperors Deming, Xuanyuan, and Xingsheng, all of whom had temples established in the capital;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted them styled di as well; the ministers then cited the precedents of Emperors Deming, Xuanyuan, and Xingsheng, all of whom had temples in the capital;

sentences.zh: 帝令立於應州舊宅，自高祖考妣以下皆追謚曰皇帝、皇后，墓曰陵。

translations.literal: the emperor ordered them established at the old residence in Yingzhou; from the High Ancestor's father and mother downward all were posthumously titled Emperor and Empress, and tombs were called mausoleums.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor ordered the temples built at the old family residence in Yingzhou. From the High Ancestor's parents downward, all forebears were posthumously titled emperor and empress, and their tombs were styled mausoleums.

sentences.zh: 漢主如康州。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han went to Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han traveled to Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蔚、代緣邊粟鬥不過十錢。

translations.literal: This year, along the borders of Yu and Dai, grain per dou did not exceed ten cash.
translations.idiomatic: That year grain along the Yu and Dai frontier sold for no more than ten cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝中之上天成三年（

translations.literal: Middle section of Emperor Mingzong the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Filially Pious—upper part, Tiancheng year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Filially Pious—middle section, upper part: Tiancheng year 3 (

sentences.zh: 戊子，公元九二八年）

translations.literal: wuzi, CE 928)
translations.idiomatic: wuzi, 928 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁巳，吳主立子璉為江都王，璘為江夏王，璆為宜春王，宣帝子廬陵公玢為南陽王。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on dingsi, the Wu ruler enfeoffed his son Lian as Prince of Jiangdu, Lin as Prince of Jiangxia, Qiu as Prince of Yichun, and the Accomplished Emperor's son, Duke of Luling Bin, as Prince of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on dingsi the Wu emperor enfeoffed his son Lian as Prince of Jiangdu, Lin as Prince of Jiangxia, Qiu as Prince of Yichun, and the Accomplished Emperor's son Bin, Duke of Luling, as Prince of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使毛璋所為驕僭，時報赭袍，縱酒為戲，左右有諫者，剖其心而視之。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi military governor Mao Zhang's conduct was arrogant and presumptuous; he often reported wearing the ochre robe, indulged in wine as sport, and when those beside him remonstrated, he cut open their hearts to look.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zhang, military governor of Zhaoyi, behaved with arrogant presumption. He often reported wearing an imperial ochre robe, drank heavily for amusement, and when attendants remonstrated with him, he cut open their hearts to inspect them.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，征為右金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he summoned him to serve as General-in-Chief of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On learning of this, the emperor recalled him to court as general-in-chief of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 契丹陷平州。

translations.literal: The Khitan captured Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan captured Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day dingchou of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon of dingchou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 帝將如鄴都，時扈駕諸軍家屬甫遷大梁，又聞將如鄴都，皆不悅，哅哅有流言。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to go to Yedu; at that time the families of the various armies accompanying the throne had just moved to Daliang, and on hearing he would go to Yedu, all were displeased, murmuring with slanderous talk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor planned to travel to Yedu. The families of the armies accompanying the court had only just been relocated to Daliang, and when they heard he would move on to Yedu, they were discontented and spread angry rumors.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，不果行。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he did not in the end go.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he abandoned the journey.

sentences.zh: 吳自莊宗滅梁以來，使者往來不絕。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, envoys between Wu and the court had come and gone without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Since Emperor Zhuangzong's destruction of Liang, diplomatic exchanges with Wu had never ceased.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，吳使者至，安重誨以為楊敢與朝廷抗禮，遣使窺覘，拒而不受，自是遂與吳絕。

translations.literal: On gengchen, a Wu envoy arrived; An Chonghui thought Yang dared to contend in ceremony with the court, sent an envoy to observe and spy, and refused to receive him—from this time relations with Wu were severed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen a Wu envoy arrived. An Chonghui, believing Yang dared to treat the court as an equal, sent an observer to reconnoiter and then refused to receive the envoy. From that point diplomatic ties with Wu were cut.

sentences.zh: 張筠至長安，守兵閉門拒之；

translations.literal: Zhang Yun reached Chang'an; the garrison troops closed the gates and refused him;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yun reached Chang'an, the garrison closed the gates against him;

sentences.zh: 筠單騎入朝，以為左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Yun entered court alone on horseback and was made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yun rode alone to court and was appointed general-in-chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，寧江節度使西方鄴攻拔歸州；

translations.literal: On renchen, Ningjiang military governor Xi Fangye attacked and captured Guizhou;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Xi Fangye, military governor of Ningjiang, attacked and captured Guizhou;

sentences.zh: 未幾，荊南復取之。

translations.literal: before long, Jingnan recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: before long Jingnan recovered it.

sentences.zh: 樞密使、同平章事孔循，性狡佞，安重誨親信之。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Concurrent Associate Chief Minister Kong Xun was by nature crafty and sycophantic; An Chonghui trusted him closely.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and associate chief minister, was crafty and sycophantic by nature, and An Chonghui trusted him deeply.

sentences.zh: 帝欲為皇子娶重誨女，循謂重誨曰：「公職居近密，不宜復與皇子為婚。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to marry a prince to Chonghui's daughter; Xun said to Chonghui, "Your office lies in the innermost secrecy—it is not fitting to marry again into the imperial clan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to marry one of his sons to Chonghui's daughter. Xun told Chonghui, "Your post is at the heart of state secrets—it is unwise to marry into the imperial family as well."

sentences.zh: 重誨辭之。

translations.literal: Chonghui declined.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui declined.

sentences.zh: 久之，或謂重誨曰：「循善離間人，不可置之密地。」

translations.literal: After a long while, someone said to Chonghui, "Xun is skilled at sowing discord among people—he must not be kept in a secret post."
translations.idiomatic: After some time someone told Chonghui, "Xun is adept at driving wedges between people—he should not hold a post at the inner court."

sentences.zh: 循知之，陰遣人結王德妃，求納其女；

translations.literal: Xun learned of this and secretly sent men to befriend Consort Wang of Virtue, seeking to have his daughter accepted;
translations.idiomatic: Xun learned of this and secretly sent agents to cultivate Consort Wang of Virtue, seeking a marriage for his daughter;

sentences.zh: 德妃請娶循女為從厚婦，帝許之。

translations.literal: the consort requested that Xun's daughter be taken as wife for Conghou; the emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: the consort asked that Xun's daughter marry Conghou, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 重誨大怒，乙未，以循同平章事，充忠武節度使兼東都留守。

translations.literal: Chonghui was greatly enraged; on yimao, Xun was made Concurrent Associate Chief Minister, filling the post of Zhongwu military governor and Eastern Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui was furious. On yimao Xun was appointed associate chief minister and sent out as military governor of Zhongwu and garrison commander of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 重誨性強愎。

translations.literal: Chonghui was by nature forceful and obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui was forceful and obstinate by nature.

sentences.zh: 秦州節度使華溫琪入朝，請留闕下，帝嘉之，除左驍衛上將軍，月別賜錢穀。

translations.literal: Qinzhou military governor Hua Wenqi entered court and requested to remain at the capital; the emperor commended this, appointed him General-in-Chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard, and granted money and grain monthly apart from salary.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Wenqi, military governor of Qinzhou, came to court and asked to remain at the capital. The emperor approved, appointed him general-in-chief of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard, and granted him a separate monthly stipend in cash and grain.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，帝謂重誨曰：「溫琪舊人，宜擇一重鎮處之。」

translations.literal: After more than a year, the emperor said to Chonghui, "Wenqi is an old companion—he should be placed in some weighty frontier command."
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the emperor told Chonghui, "Wenqi is an old companion of mine—he ought to be given a major frontier post."

sentences.zh: 重誨對以無闕。

translations.literal: Chonghui replied that there were no vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui replied that no posts were vacant.

sentences.zh: 他日，帝屢言之，重誨慍曰：「臣累奏無闕，惟樞密使可代耳。」

translations.literal: On another day the emperor spoke of it repeatedly; Chonghui said angrily, "Your servant has repeatedly memorialized that there are no vacancies—only the commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs could be replaced."
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor raised the matter again. Chonghui snapped, "I have told Your Majesty repeatedly that nothing is open—only the post of commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs could serve."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「亦可。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "That too will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That will do as well."

sentences.zh: 重誨無以對。

translations.literal: Chonghui had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui had no answer.

sentences.zh: 溫琪聞之懼，數月不出。

translations.literal: Wenqi heard of this and was afraid, and for several months did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenqi heard of this, he was terrified and did not leave his residence for months.

sentences.zh: 重誨惡成德節度使、同平章事王建立，奏建立與王都交結，有異志。

translations.literal: Chonghui hated Chengde military governor and Concurrent Associate Chief Minister Wang Jianli and memorialized that Jianli was in league with Wang Du and harbored divergent intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui hated Wang Jianli, military governor of Chengde and associate chief minister, and memorialized that Jianli was conspiring with Wang Du and harbored rebellious designs.

sentences.zh: 建立亦奏重誨專權，求入朝面言其狀，帝召之。

translations.literal: Jianli also memorialized that Chonghui monopolized power, requested to enter court and speak of the matter face to face, and the emperor summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli also accused Chonghui of monopolizing power and asked to come to court to speak in person; the emperor summoned him.

sentences.zh: 既至，言重誨與宣徽使判三司張延朗結婚，相表裡，弄威福。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he said Chonghui had married into the family of Palace Secretariat commissioner and acting Three Departments director Zhang Yanlang, that they supported each other inside and out, and manipulated authority and favor.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he charged that Chonghui had married into the family of Zhang Yanlang, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and acting director of the Three Departments, that they backed each other, and together abused their power.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛亥，帝見重誨，氣色甚怒，謂曰：「今與卿一鎮自休息，以王建立代卿，張延朗亦除外官。」

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinhai, the emperor received Chonghui, his expression very angry, and said, "Now I give you a command to rest yourself; Wang Jianli will replace you, and Zhang Yanlang will also be sent out as an outer official."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinhai, the emperor received Chonghui in a fury and said, "I am giving you a frontier post where you can rest. Wang Jianli will replace you, and Zhang Yanlang will be sent out of court as well."

sentences.zh: 重誨曰：「臣披荊棘事陛下數十年，值陛下龍飛，承乏機密，數年間天下幸無事。

translations.literal: Chonghui said, "Your servant cleared thorns to serve Your Majesty for decades; when Your Majesty's dragon flew aloft, I filled the post of secret affairs, and for several years under Heaven fortunately there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui said, "I have cut through thorns to serve Your Majesty for decades. When you ascended the throne I took charge of secret affairs, and for years the realm has been fortunate to know peace.

sentences.zh: 今一旦棄之外鎮，臣願聞其罪！」

translations.literal: Now in a single morning I am cast out to an outer command—I wish to hear my crime!"
translations.idiomatic: Now, in a single stroke, I am cast out to the frontier. At least tell me my crime!"

sentences.zh: 帝不懌而起，以語宣徽使朱弘昭，弘昭曰：「陛下平日待重誨如左右手，奈何以小忿棄之！

translations.literal: The emperor rose displeased and told Palace Secretariat commissioner Zhu Hongzhao; Hongzhao said, "Your Majesty on ordinary days treats Chonghui like right hand and left—how can you abandon him over a small resentment!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rose in displeasure and told Zhu Hongzhao, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat. Hongzhao said, "Your Majesty has always treated Chonghui like your own hands—how can you cast him aside over a petty grievance!

sentences.zh: 願垂三思。」

translations.literal: I beg you to reflect thrice."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to think again."

sentences.zh: 帝尋召重誨慰撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor soon summoned Chonghui back and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon summoned Chonghui back and reassured him.

sentences.zh: 明日，建立辭歸鎮，帝曰：「卿比奏欲入分朕憂，今復去何之！」

translations.literal: The next day Jianli took leave to return to his command; the emperor said, "You recently memorialized wishing to enter court to share my cares—now you go again, whither!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jianli asked leave to return to his post. The emperor said, "You recently asked to come to court and share my burdens—where are you going now!"

sentences.zh: 會門下侍郎兼刑部尚書、同平章事鄭玨請致仕；

translations.literal: It happened that Vice Director of the Secretariat, Concurrent Minister of Justice, and Associate Chief Minister Zheng Jue requested retirement;
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Zheng Jue, vice director of the Secretariat, minister of justice, and associate chief minister, asked to retire;

sentences.zh: 己未，以玨為左僕射致仕，癸亥，以建立為右僕射兼中書侍郎、同平章事、判三司。

translations.literal: on jiwei, Jue was made Retired Left Grand Counselor; on guihai, Jianli was made Right Grand Counselor with concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat, Associate Chief Minister, and acting Three Departments director.
translations.idiomatic: on jiwei Jue was appointed retired left grand counselor; on guihai Jianli was made right grand counselor, vice director of the Secretariat, associate chief minister, and acting director of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥屢與董璋爭鹽利，璋誘商旅販東川鹽入西川，知祥患之，乃於漢州置三場重征之，歲得錢七萬緡，商旅不復之東川。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang repeatedly contended with Dong Zhang over salt profits; Zhang enticed merchants to sell Dongchuan salt into Xichuan; Zhixiang was troubled by this and therefore established three stations at Hanzhou to levy heavy taxes, gaining seventy thousand strings per year, and merchants no longer went to Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang repeatedly clashed over salt revenues. Zhang lured merchants to sell Dongchuan salt in Xichuan, which troubled Zhixiang. He set up three tax stations at Hanzhou with heavy levies, collecting seventy thousand strings a year and diverting merchants away from Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷如岳州，遣六軍使袁詮、副使王環、監軍馬希瞻將水軍擊荊南，高季興以水軍逆戰。

translations.literal: King Yin of Chu went to Yuezhou and dispatched Six Armies commissioner Yuan Quan, deputy commissioner Wang Huan, and supervising general Ma Xizhan to lead the naval force against Jingnan; Gao Jixing met them on the water in battle.
translations.idiomatic: King Yin of Chu traveled to Yuezhou and sent Yuan Quan, commissioner of the Six Armies, his deputy Wang Huan, and supervising general Ma Xizhan to attack Jingnan by water. Gao Jixing met them with his own fleet.

sentences.zh: 至劉郎洑，希瞻夜匿戰艦數十艘於港中；

translations.literal: Reaching Liulangpu, Xizhan by night hid several tens of warships in the harbor;
translations.idiomatic: At Liulangpu, Xizhan hid several dozen warships in the harbor by night;

sentences.zh: 詰旦，兩軍合戰，希瞻出戰艦橫擊之，季興大敗，俘斬以千數，進逼江陵。

translations.literal: at dawn the two armies joined battle; Xizhan brought out the warships and struck across them; Jixing was greatly defeated, captives and slain numbered in the thousands, and they pressed on toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: at dawn the two fleets engaged. Xizhan brought his hidden ships out in a flanking attack. Jixing was routed; captives and dead numbered in the thousands, and the Chu army pressed toward Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 季興請和，歸史光憲於楚。

translations.literal: Jixing requested peace and returned Shi Guangxian to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing sued for peace and returned Shi Guangxian to Chu.

sentences.zh: 軍還，楚王殷讓環不遂取荊南，環曰：「江陵在中朝及吳、蜀之間，四戰之地也，宜存之以為吾扞蔽。」

translations.literal: When the army returned, King Yin of Chu reproached Huan for not finishing the seizure of Jingnan; Huan said, "Jiangling lies between the Central Court and Wu and Shu—a place of battle on four sides; it should be preserved as our shield and screen."
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, King Yin reproached Huan for failing to take Jingnan. Huan said, "Jiangling lies between the central court, Wu, and Shu—a crossroads of war. We should keep it alive as our buffer."

sentences.zh: 殷說。

translations.literal: Yin was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 環每戰，身先士卒，與從同甘苦；

translations.literal: In every battle Huan took the lead before the soldiers and shared hardship and ease with his followers;
translations.idiomatic: In every battle Huan led from the front and shared hardship with his men;

sentences.zh: 常置針藥於座右，戰罷，索傷者於帳前，自傅治之。

translations.literal: he always placed needles and medicine by his seat; when battle ended, he sought the wounded before his tent and personally applied treatment.
translations.idiomatic: he kept needles and medicine at his side, and after each fight summoned the wounded to his tent and dressed their wounds himself.

sentences.zh: 士卒隸環麾下者相賀曰：「吾屬得死所矣。」

translations.literal: Soldiers under Huan's command congratulated one another, saying, "We have found the place to die."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers under his command congratulated one another: "We have found the place where we would choose to die."

sentences.zh: 故所向有功。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever they went they achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: That is why they won wherever they fought.

sentences.zh: 楚大舉水軍擊漢，圍封州。

translations.literal: Chu launched a major naval attack on Han and besieged Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chu mounted a major naval campaign against Han and besieged Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢主以《周易》筮之，遇《大有》，於是大赦，改元大有；

translations.literal: The ruler of Han divined with the Book of Changes and obtained Great Possession; thereupon he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Dayou;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han divined with the Book of Changes and obtained the hexagram Great Possession. He thereupon proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Dayou;

sentences.zh: 命左右街使蘇章將神弩三千、戰艦百艘救封州。

translations.literal: he ordered Left and Right Street commissioner Su Zhang to lead three thousand divine crossbows and a hundred warships to relieve Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Su Zhang, commissioner of the Left and Right Streets, to lead three thousand crossbowmen and a hundred warships to relieve Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 章至賀江，沉鐵絲亙於水，兩岸作巨輪挽絲亙，築長堤以隱之，伏壯士於堤中。

translations.literal: Zhang reached He River, sank iron cables across the water, built great wheels on both banks to draw the cables taut, constructed a long dike to conceal them, and hid stalwarts within the dike.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang reached the He River, sank iron cables across the channel, mounted great wheels on both banks to haul them taut, built a long dike to conceal the trap, and hid warriors inside it.

sentences.zh: 章以輕舟逆戰，陽不利，楚人逐之，入堤中；

translations.literal: Zhang fought with light boats in reverse, feigning disadvantage; the men of Chu pursued them into the dike;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang engaged with light boats and feigned defeat. The Chu fleet pursued them into the dike;

sentences.zh: 挽輪舉緪，楚艦不能進退，以強弩夾水射之，楚兵大敗，解圍遁去。

translations.literal: the wheels were turned and the cables raised; Chu warships could neither advance nor retreat; powerful crossbows shot from both sides of the water; Chu troops were greatly defeated and raised the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: the wheels were turned and the cables raised, trapping the Chu ships. Powerful crossbows fired from both banks. The Chu army was shattered, lifted the siege, and fled.

sentences.zh: 漢主以章為封州團練使。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han made Zhang regimental commissioner of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Han appointed Zhang regimental commissioner of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以鄴都留守從榮為河東節度使、北都留守，以客省使太原馮贇為副留守，夾馬指揮使新平楊思權為步軍都指揮使以佐之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Yedu garrison commander Congrong was made Hedong military governor and Northern Capital garrison commander; Guest Affairs commissioner Feng Yun of Taiyuan was made deputy garrison commander; and Jia Ma commander Yang Siquan of Xinping was made infantry commander-in-chief to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Congrong, garrison commander of Yedu, was appointed military governor of Hedong and garrison commander of the Northern Capital, with Feng Yun of Taiyuan as deputy garrison commander and Yang Siquan of Xinping, commander of the Jia Ma guard, as infantry commander-in-chief to assist him.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以宣武節度使石敬瑭為鄴都留守、天雄節度使，加同平章事；

translations.literal: On wuyin, Xuanwu military governor Shi Jingtang was made Yedu garrison commander and Tianxiong military governor, with added rank of Associate Chief Minister;
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Shi Jingtang, military governor of Xuanwu, was appointed garrison commander of Yedu and military governor of Tianxiong, with the added rank of associate chief minister;

sentences.zh: 以樞密使范延光為成德節度使。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Fan Yanguang was made Chengde military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made military governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以樞密使安重誨兼河南尹，以河南尹從厚為宣武節度使，仍判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs An Chonghui was additionally made Henan metropolitan prefect; Henan metropolitan prefect Conghou was made Xuanwu military governor and still directed the Six Armies and various guards.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu An Chonghui, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was also made metropolitan prefect of Henan; Conghou, metropolitan prefect of Henan, was appointed military governor of Xuanwu while retaining direction of the Six Armies and palace guards.

sentences.zh: 吳右雄武軍使苗璘、靜江統軍王彥章將水軍萬人攻楚岳州，至君山，楚王殷遣右丞相許德勳將戰艦千艘御之。

translations.literal: Wu Right Valiant Martial Army commissioner Miao Lin and Jingjiang commander-in-chief Wang Yanzhang led ten thousand men in a naval attack on Chu's Yuezhou; reaching Jun Mountain, King Yin of Chu dispatched Right Chief Minister Xu Dexun with a thousand warships to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Lin, commissioner of Wu's Right Valiant Martial Army, and Wang Yanzhang, commander-in-chief of Jingjiang, led ten thousand men by water against Yuezhou in Chu. At Jun Mountain, King Yin sent Xu Dexun, his right chief minister, with a thousand warships to meet them.

sentences.zh: 德勳曰：「吳人掩吾不備，見大軍，必懼而走。」

translations.literal: Dexun said, "The men of Wu struck us unprepared; when they see a great army, they will surely fear and flee."
translations.idiomatic: Dexun said, "Wu caught us off guard, but when they see a large fleet they will panic and run."

sentences.zh: 乃潛軍角子湖，使王環夜帥戰艦三百，屯楊林浦，絕吳歸路。

translations.literal: He therefore concealed troops at Jiaozi Lake and had Wang Huan by night lead three hundred warships to encamp at Yanglin Ford, cutting off Wu's route of return.
translations.idiomatic: He hid his main force at Jiaozi Lake and sent Wang Huan with three hundred warships by night to Yanglin Ford, cutting off Wu's retreat.

sentences.zh: 遲明，吳人進軍荊江口，將會荊南兵攻岳州，丁亥，至道人磯。

translations.literal: Near dawn the men of Wu advanced to the Jing River mouth, intending to join Jingnan troops to attack Yuezhou; on dinghai they reached Daoren Rock.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn the Wu fleet advanced to the mouth of the Jing River, intending to join Jingnan forces against Yuezhou. On dinghai they reached Daoren Rock.

sentences.zh: 德勳命戰棹都虞侯詹信以輕舟三百出吳軍後，德勳以大軍當其前，夾擊之，吳軍大敗，虜璘及彥章以歸。

translations.literal: Dexun ordered Battle Oar chief inspector Zhan Xin with three hundred light boats to come out behind the Wu army; Dexun with the great army blocked them in front; they struck from both sides; the Wu army was greatly defeated, and Lin and Yanzhang were captured and brought back.
translations.idiomatic: Dexun ordered Zhan Xin, chief inspector of the battle oars, to take three hundred light boats around the Wu rear while he blocked them in front with the main fleet. Caught between the two forces, Wu was routed. Lin and Yanzhang were captured and brought back.

sentences.zh: 初，義武節度使兼中書令王都鎮易定十餘年，自除刺史以下官，租賦皆贍本軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yiwu military governor and Concurrent Palace Secretariat Director Wang Du had governed Yi and Ding for more than ten years, himself appointing officials from prefect downward, and rents and taxes all supplied his own army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Du, military governor of Yiwu and palace secretariat director, had ruled Yi and Ding for more than ten years, appointing his own officials down to the prefectural level and keeping all taxes for his army.

sentences.zh: 及安重誨用事，稍以法制裁之；

translations.literal: When An Chonghui came to power, he gradually restrained him by statute and regulation;
translations.idiomatic: When An Chonghui came to power, the court gradually restrained him with imperial law;

sentences.zh: 帝亦以都篡父位，惡之。

translations.literal: the emperor also, because Du had usurped his father's position, detested him.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor also despised him for having seized power from his father.

sentences.zh: 時契丹數犯塞，朝廷多屯兵於幽、易間，大將往來，都陰為之備，浸成猜阻。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan repeatedly raided the frontier; the court stationed many troops between You and Yi; great generals came and went; Du secretly made preparations against them, and suspicion and obstruction gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were raiding the frontier repeatedly, and the court massed troops between You and Yi. As senior generals came and went, Du made secret preparations against them, and mutual suspicion grew.

sentences.zh: 都恐朝遷移之它鎮，腹心和昭訓勸都為自全之計，都乃求婚於盧龍節度使趙德鈞。

translations.literal: Du feared the court would transfer him to another command; his intimate He Zhaoxun urged Du to plan for self-preservation; Du thereupon sought a marriage alliance with Lulong military governor Zhao Dejun.
translations.idiomatic: Du feared transfer to another post. His confidant He Zhaoxun urged him to secure his position, and Du sought a marriage alliance with Zhao Dejun, military governor of Lulong.

sentences.zh: 又知成德節度使王建立與安重誨有隙，遣使結為兄弟，陰與之謀復河北故事，建立陽許而密奏之。

translations.literal: He also knew Chengde military governor Wang Jianli was at odds with An Chonghui, sent envoys to bond as sworn brothers, and secretly plotted with him to restore the old Hebei arrangement; Jianli outwardly agreed but secretly memorialized this.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Wang Jianli of Chengde was at odds with An Chonghui, he sent envoys to swear brotherhood and secretly plotted to restore the old Hebei autonomy. Jianli pretended to agree but reported the plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 都又以蠟書遺青、徐、潞、益、梓五帥，離間之。

translations.literal: Du also sent sealed letters to the five commanders of Qing, Xu, Lu, Yi, and Zi, sowing division among them.
translations.idiomatic: Du also sent sealed letters to the military governors of Qing, Xu, Lu, Yi, and Zi, seeking to turn them against the court.

sentences.zh: 又遣人說北面副招討使歸德節度使王晏球，晏球不從；

translations.literal: He also sent men to persuade Northern Deputy Campaign Commissioner and Guide military governor Wang Yanqiu; Yanqiu did not follow;
translations.idiomatic: He also sent agents to win over Wang Yanqiu, deputy northern campaign commissioner and military governor of Guide, but Yanqiu refused;

sentences.zh: 乃以金遺晏球帳下，使圖之，不克；

translations.literal: thereupon he gave gold to men under Yanqiu's tent, having them plot against him, but did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: he then bribed Yanqiu's subordinates to assassinate him, but the plot failed;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，晏球以都反狀聞，詔宣徽使張延朗與北面諸將議討之。

translations.literal: on guisi, Yanqiu reported Du's rebellion; an edict ordered Palace Secretariat commissioner Zhang Yanlang and the northern generals to deliberate on suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: on guisi Yanqiu reported Du's rebellion. The court ordered Zhang Yanlang, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, and the northern generals to plan the campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，吳徙常山王濛為臨川王。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Wu transferred Prince of Changshan Meng to Prince of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Wu transferred Prince Meng of Changshan to Prince of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔削奪王都官爵。

translations.literal: On gengzi, an edict stripped Wang Du of rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict stripped Wang Du of all rank and titles.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以王晏球為北面討使，權知定州行州事，以橫海節度使安審通為副招討使，以鄭州防禦使張虔釗為都監，發諸道兵會討定州。

translations.literal: On renyin, Wang Yanqiu was made Northern Suppression Commissioner with acting authority over Dingzhou administrative affairs; Heng Hai military governor An Shentong was made deputy campaign commissioner; Zhengzhou defense commissioner Zhang Qianzhao was made overall supervisor; troops from all circuits were mobilized to join in attacking Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Wang Yanqiu was appointed northern suppression commissioner with acting authority over Dingzhou. An Shentong, military governor of Heng Hai, was made deputy campaign commissioner; Zhang Qianzhao, defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, was overall supervisor; and troops from all circuits were mobilized against Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，晏球攻定州，拔其北關城。

translations.literal: That same day Yanqiu attacked Dingzhou and captured its North Gate city.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yanqiu attacked Dingzhou and took its North Gate quarter.

sentences.zh: 都以重賂求救於奚酋禿餒，五月，禿餒以萬騎突入定州，晏球退保曲陽，都與禿餒就攻之。

translations.literal: Du with heavy bribes sought rescue from Xi chieftain Tuyu; in the fifth month Tuyu with ten thousand horsemen burst into Dingzhou; Yanqiu withdrew to defend Quyang; Du joined Tuyu in pressing the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Du sent rich bribes to the Xi chieftain Tuyu. In the fifth month Tuyu burst into Dingzhou with ten thousand horsemen. Yanqiu fell back to Quyang, and Du joined Tuyu in attacking him.

sentences.zh: 晏球與戰於嘉山下，大破之。

translations.literal: Yanqiu fought them beneath Jia Mountain and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu met them below Jia Mountain and routed them.

sentences.zh: 禿餒以二千騎奔還定州。

translations.literal: Tuyu with two thousand horsemen fled back to Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyu fled back to Dingzhou with two thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 晏球追至城門，因進攻之，得其西關城。

translations.literal: Yanqiu pursued to the city gate and thereupon pressed the attack, capturing its West Gate city.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu pursued to the city gate and pressed the attack, taking the West Gate quarter.

sentences.zh: 定州城堅，不可攻，晏球增修西關城以為行府，使三州民輸稅供軍食而守之。

translations.literal: Dingzhou's walls were strong and could not be stormed; Yanqiu enlarged and repaired the West Gate city as his field headquarters, had the people of three prefectures deliver taxes to supply army provisions, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzhou's walls were too strong to storm. Yanqiu fortified the West Gate quarter as his field headquarters, levied grain from three prefectures to feed his army, and settled in for a siege.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以天雄節度副使趙敬怡為樞密使。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Tianxiong military governor deputy Zhao Jingyi was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Zhao Jingyi, deputy military governor of Tianxiong, was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 王晏球聞契丹發兵救定州，將大軍趣望都，遣張延朗分兵退保新樂，延朗遂之真定，留趙州刺史朱建豐將兵修新樂城。

translations.literal: Wang Yanqiu heard the Khitan were sending troops to rescue Dingzhou, led his great army toward Wangdu, and dispatched Zhang Yanlang with divided forces to withdraw and defend Xinle; Yanlang thereupon went to Zhending and left Zhaozhou prefect Zhu Jianfeng to lead troops in repairing Xinle's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Khitan were marching to relieve Dingzhou, Wang Yanqiu led his main force toward Wangdu and sent Zhang Yanlang with a detachment to hold Xinle. Yanlang went on to Zhending and left Zhu Jianfeng, prefect of Zhaozhou, to repair the walls of Xinle.

sentences.zh: 契丹已自他道入定州，與王都夜襲新樂，破之，殺建豐。

translations.literal: The Khitan had already entered Dingzhou by another route; with Wang Du they raided Xinle by night, broke it, and killed Jianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had already entered Dingzhou by another route. With Wang Du they raided Xinle by night, overran it, and killed Jianfeng.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，王晏球、張延朗會於行唐，丙寅，至曲陽。

translations.literal: On yichou, Wang Yanqiu and Zhang Yanlang joined at Xingtang; on bingyin they reached Quyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Yanqiu and Yanlang rendezvoused at Xingtang; on bingyin they reached Quyang.

sentences.zh: 王都乘勝，悉其眾與契丹五千騎合萬餘人，邀晏球等於曲陽，丁卯，戰於城南。

translations.literal: Wang Du, riding his victory, mustered all his forces and with five thousand Khitan horsemen totaled more than ten thousand men, intercepted Yanqiu and the others at Quyang, and on dingmao fought south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du, pressing his advantage, mustered his entire force and joined five thousand Khitan horsemen for more than ten thousand men. He intercepted Yanqiu at Quyang, and on dingmao they fought south of the city.

sentences.zh: 晏球集諸將校令之曰：「王都輕而驕，可一戰擒也。

translations.literal: Yanqiu assembled the generals and officers and ordered them, saying, "Wang Du is light and arrogant—he can be captured in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu assembled his officers and said, "Wang Du is reckless and arrogant. We can take him in one battle.

sentences.zh: 今日，諸君報國之時也。

translations.literal: Today is the time for you gentlemen to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Today is the day to repay your country.

sentences.zh: 悉去弓矢，以短兵擊之，回顧者斬！」

translations.literal: Cast aside all bows and arrows; strike them with short weapons; whoever looks back shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Cast aside your bows and strike with edged weapons. Anyone who turns back will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 於是騎兵先進，奮，楇揮劍，直衝其陳，大破之，殭屍蔽野；

translations.literal: Thereupon the cavalry advanced first, striving fiercely; Yanqiu waved his sword and charged straight into their formation; they were greatly defeated, corpses covering the field;
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry charged first. Yanqiu waved his sword and drove straight into the enemy line. The foe was shattered, and corpses covered the field;

sentences.zh: 契丹死者過半，餘眾北走；

translations.literal: of the Khitan more than half died, the remainder fled north;
translations.idiomatic: more than half the Khitan were killed and the rest fled north;

sentences.zh: 都與禿餒得數騎，僅免。

translations.literal: Du and Tuyu obtained only a few horsemen and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Du and Tuyu escaped with only a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使趙德鈞邀擊契丹，北走者殆無孑遺。

translations.literal: Lulong military governor Zhao Dejun intercepted and struck the Khitan; of those fleeing north scarcely one survived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dejun, military governor of Lulong, intercepted the fleeing Khitan, and scarcely a man escaped north alive.

sentences.zh: 吳遣使求和於楚，請苗璘、王彥章；

translations.literal: Wu sent envoys seeking peace with Chu, requesting Miao Lin and Wang Yanzhang;
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent envoys to sue for peace with Chu and asked for the return of Miao Lin and Wang Yanzhang;

sentences.zh: 楚王殷歸之，使許德勳餞之。

translations.literal: King Yin of Chu returned them and had Xu Dexun give them a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: King Yin released them and had Xu Dexun host a farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 德勳謂二人曰：「楚國雖小，舊臣宿將猶在，願吳朝勿以措懷。

translations.literal: Dexun said to the two, "Though Chu is small, old ministers and veteran generals still remain—I hope the Wu court will not take this to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Dexun told the two men, "Chu may be small, but its old ministers and veteran generals remain. I hope the Wu court will not take offense.

sentences.zh: 必俟眾駒爭皁棧，然後可圖也。」

translations.literal: You must wait until the many colts contend for the manger—only then can it be plotted."
translations.idiomatic: You must wait until the young stallions fight over the manger—only then will there be an opening."

sentences.zh: 時殷多內寵，嫡庶無別，諸子驕奢，故德勳語及之。

translations.literal: At that time Yin had many inner favorites, made no distinction between legitimate and illegitimate sons, and his sons were arrogant and extravagant—therefore Dexun spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yin favored many consorts, made no distinction between legitimate and illegitimate sons, and his sons were arrogant and extravagant—hence Dexun's remark.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛巳，高季興復請稱籓於吳，吳進季興爵秦王，帝詔楚王殷討之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on xinsi, Gao Jixing again requested to declare himself vassal to Wu; Wu advanced Jixing's rank to Prince of Qin; the emperor ordered King Yin of Chu to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on xinsi, Gao Jixing again submitted to Wu as a vassal. Wu enfeoffed him as Prince of Qin. The Later Tang emperor ordered King Yin of Chu to attack him.

sentences.zh: 殷遣許德勳將兵攻荊南，以其子希範為監軍，次沙頭。

translations.literal: Yin dispatched Xu Dexun to lead troops against Jingnan, with his son Xifan as supervising general, encamped at Shatou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent Xu Dexun against Jingnan with his son Xifan as supervising general, encamping at Shatou.

sentences.zh: 季興從子雲猛指揮使從嗣單騎造楚壁，請與希範挑戰決勝，副指揮使廖匡齊出與之鬥，拉殺之。

translations.literal: Jixing's nephew, Cloud Fierce commander Congsi, came alone on horseback to the Chu camp, requesting to challenge Xifan to decisive combat; deputy commander Liao Kuangqi came out to duel with him and pulled him down and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing's nephew Congsi, commander of Cloud Fierce, rode alone to the Chu camp and challenged Xifan to single combat. Deputy commander Liao Kuangqi accepted the duel, dragged him from his horse, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 季興懼，明日，請和，德勳還。

translations.literal: Jixing was afraid; the next day he requested peace, and Dexun returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jixing was terrified. The next day he sued for peace, and Dexun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 匡齊，贛人也。

translations.literal: Kuangqi was a man of Gan.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangqi was a native of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 王晏球知定州有備，未易急攻，朱弘昭、張虔釗宣言大將畏怯，有詔促令攻城。

translations.literal: Wang Yanqiu knew Dingzhou was prepared and not easy to storm quickly; Zhu Hongzhao and Zhang Qianzhao proclaimed that the great generals were timid and cowardly; there was an edict urging them to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanqiu knew Dingzhou was well defended and could not be rushed. Zhu Hongzhao and Zhang Qianzhao spread word that the generals were timid, and an edict pressed them to assault the city.

sentences.zh: 晏球不得已，乙未，攻之，殺傷將士三千人。

translations.literal: Yanqiu had no choice; on yimao he attacked; three thousand officers and soldiers were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu had no choice. On yimao he attacked, losing three thousand officers and men killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔發西川兵戍夔州，孟知祥遣左肅邊指揮使毛重威將三千人往。

translations.literal: Earlier, an edict ordered Xichuan troops garrisoned at Qizhou; Meng Zhixiang dispatched Left Border Pacification commander Mao Chongwei to lead three thousand men there.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had ordered Xichuan troops to garrison Qizhou. Meng Zhixiang sent Mao Chongwei, commander of the Left Border Pacification guard, with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 頃之，知祥奏「夔、忠、萬三州已平，請召戍兵還，以省饋運。」

translations.literal: Before long Zhixiang memorialized, "The three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan are already pacified—I request the garrison troops be recalled to save transport costs."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhixiang memorialized that the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan were pacified and asked that the garrison be recalled to save transport costs."

sentences.zh: 帝不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not grant this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 知祥陰使人誘之，重威帥其眾鼓噪逃歸。

translations.literal: Zhixiang secretly sent men to entice them; Chongwei led his masses in clamor and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang secretly sent agents to incite them. Chongwei led his men in a clamorous mutiny and marched home.

sentences.zh: 帝命按其罪，知祥請而免之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered his crime investigated; Zhixiang requested and secured his pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him punished, but Zhixiang interceded and secured his pardon.

sentences.zh: 陝州行軍司馬王宗壽請葬故蜀主王衍，秋，七月，乙巳，贈衍順正公，以諸侯禮葬之。

translations.literal: Shaanzhou acting military governor Wang Zongshou requested burial for the former Shu ruler Wang Yan; in autumn, the seventh month, on yisi, Yan was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Shunzheng and buried with the rites of a feudal lord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongshou, acting military governor of Shaanzhou, asked to bury the former Shu ruler Wang Yan. In autumn, the seventh month, on yisi, Yan was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Shunzheng and buried with feudal honors.

sentences.zh: 北面招討使安審通卒。

translations.literal: Northern Campaign Commissioner An Shentong died.
translations.idiomatic: An Shentong, northern campaign commissioner, died.

sentences.zh: 東都民有犯私麴者，留守孔循族之。

translations.literal: Among Eastern Capital commoners was one who violated the private yeast ban; garrison commander Kong Xun exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: When an Eastern Capital resident violated the private brewing ban, garrison commander Kong Xun executed his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 或請聽民造麴，而於秋稅畝收五錢；

translations.literal: some requested allowing the people to brew yeast and collecting five cash per mu in autumn tax;
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed allowing private brewing and collecting five cash per mu of autumn tax instead;

sentences.zh: 己未，敕從之。

translations.literal: on jiwei, an edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: on jiwei an edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，契丹復遣其酋長惕隱將七千騎救定州，王晏球逆戰於唐河北，大破之；

translations.literal: On renxu, the Khitan again sent their chieftain Tiyin with seven thousand horsemen to rescue Dingzhou; Wang Yanqiu met them in battle on the north bank of the Tang River and greatly defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the Khitan again sent the chieftain Tiyin with seven thousand horsemen to relieve Dingzhou. Wang Yanqiu met them on the north bank of the Tang River and routed them;

sentences.zh: 甲子，追至易州，時久雨水漲，契丹為唐所俘斬及陷溺死者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: on jiazi pursued to Yizhou; at that time long rains had swollen the waters; Khitan captured, beheaded, and drowned by Tang forces were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: on jiazi he pursued to Yizhou. Prolonged rains had swollen the rivers, and Khitan killed, captured, or drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，北威武節度使王延鈞為閩王。

translations.literal: On wuchen, North Valiant Martial military governor Wang Yanjun was made King of Min.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wang Yanjun, military governor of North Valiant Martial, was enfeoffed as King of Min.

sentences.zh: 契丹北走，道路泥濘，人馬饑疲，入幽州境。

translations.literal: The Khitan fled north; roads were muddy and slick; men and horses were hungry and weary; they entered Youzhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan fled north over muddy roads, men and horses starving and exhausted, into Youzhou territory.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲戌，趙德鈞遣牙將武從諫將精騎邀擊之，分兵扼險要，生擒惕隱等數百人；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiaxu, Zhao Dejun dispatched military adjutant Wu Congjian to lead picked cavalry to intercept and strike them, divided forces to hold strategic passes, and captured alive Tiyin and several hundred others;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiaxu, Zhao Dejun sent his adjutant Wu Congjian with picked cavalry to intercept them, posted detachments at key passes, and captured Tiyin and several hundred others alive;

sentences.zh: 餘眾散投村落，村民以白梃擊之，其得脫歸國者不過數十人。

translations.literal: the remainder scattered into villages; villagers struck them with white clubs; those who escaped to return to their state were no more than several tens.
translations.idiomatic: the rest scattered into villages, where peasants beat them with clubs. Fewer than several dozen ever made it home.

sentences.zh: 自是契丹沮氣，不敢輕犯塞。

translations.literal: From this the Khitan lost their fighting spirit and did not dare lightly violate the frontier passes.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Khitan lost their nerve and no longer dared raid the border freely.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗徇地河北，獲小兒，畜之宮中，及長，賜姓名曰李繼陶；

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Zhuangzong toured the Hebei region, he captured a small boy, kept him in the palace, and when he had grown, bestowed the surname and given name Li Jitao;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Zhuangzong was campaigning in Hebei, he took in a boy he found there and raised him in the palace; when the boy came of age, Zhuangzong gave him the name Li Jitao;

sentences.zh: 帝即位，縱遣之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor assumed the throne, he released and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mingzong took the throne, he freed the man and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 王都得之，使衣黃袍坐堞間，謂王晏球曰：「此莊宗皇帝子也，已即帝位。

translations.literal: Wang Du obtained him, had him wear a yellow robe and sit among the battlements, and told Wang Yanqiu: "This is Emperor Zhuangzong's son; he has already ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du seized him, dressed him in an imperial yellow robe, and posted him on the parapets, then said to Wang Yanqiu: "This is Emperor Zhuangzong's son, and he has already taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 公受先朝厚恩，曾不念乎！」

translations.literal: You received deep grace from the former dynasty—do you not remember it at all!"
translations.idiomatic: You owe the former court a great debt—have you forgotten it entirely!

sentences.zh: 晏球曰：「此公作小數竟何益！

translations.literal: Yanqiu said: "Your lordship's petty stratagem—what good can it possibly do!
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu replied: "These little tricks of yours will do you no good whatsoever!

sentences.zh: 吾今教公二策，不悉眾決戰，則束手出降耳，自餘無以求生也。」

translations.literal: I now offer your lordship two plans: if you do not muster your entire force for a decisive battle, then simply surrender with bound hands—apart from these there is no way to live.
translations.idiomatic: I will give you two choices: either commit your full strength to one decisive battle, or surrender at once; there is no other way out.

sentences.zh: 王建立以目不知書，請罷判三司，不許。

translations.literal: Wang Jianli, on grounds that his eyes could not read writing, requested to be relieved of overseeing the Three Departments; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianli asked to be removed from his concurrent post overseeing the Three Departments on the grounds that he could not read, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 乙未，吳大赦。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Wu proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Wu issued a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐欲立中子傳瓘為嗣，謂諸子曰：「各言汝功，吾擇多者而立之。」

translations.literal: Wuyue King Qian Liu wished to install his middle son Chuanzan as heir and told his sons: "Each speak your merits; I will choose the one with the most and install him."
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu of Wuyue wanted to name his third son Chuanzan as his successor and told his sons: "Each of you describe your accomplishments; I will choose whoever has done the most and make him heir.

sentences.zh: 傳瓘兄傳璹、傳瓘、傳璟皆推傳瓘，乃奏請以兩鎮授傳瓘。

translations.literal: Chuanzan's elder brothers Chuanshu, Chuanzan, and Chuanjing all yielded to Chuanzan; they then memorialized requesting that the two circuits be granted to Chuanzan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers Chuanshu, Chuanzan, and Chuanjing all stepped aside in Chuanzan's favor, and together they submitted a request that the two circuits be granted to him.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁未，詔以傳瓘為鎮海、鎮東節度使。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on dingwei, an edict appointed Chuanzan military governor of Zhenhai and Zhendong.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on dingwei, Chuanzan was appointed military governor of both Zhenhai and Zhendong circuits.

sentences.zh: 戊申，趙德鈞獻契丹俘惕隱等，諸將皆請誅之，帝曰：「此曹皆虜中之驍將，殺之則虜絕望，不若存之以紓邊患。」

translations.literal: On wushen, Zhao Dejun presented Khitan captives including Tiyin; the generals all requested execution, and the Emperor said: "These are all fierce generals among the barbarians; killing them would leave the barbarians hopeless—better to keep them alive to ease frontier troubles."
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Zhao Dejun presented Khitan prisoners including the chieftain Tiyin. The generals all urged execution, but the emperor said: "These men are elite Khitan commanders; if we kill them the enemy will despair of reconciliation—better to spare them and so relieve pressure on the borders.

sentences.zh: 乃赦惕隱等酋長五十人，置之親衛，餘六百人悉斬之。

translations.literal: He then pardoned fifty chieftains including Tiyin, placed them in his personal guard, and had the remaining six hundred all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned fifty Khitan chieftains including Tiyin and assigned them to his personal guard, but the other six hundred captives were all executed.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣梅老季素等入貢。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent Meilaojisu and others to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan dispatched Meilaojisu and others to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 初，盧文進來降，契丹以籓漢都提舉使張希崇代之為盧龍節度使，守平州，遣親將以三百騎監之。

translations.literal: Initially, when Lu Wenjin came over in surrender, the Khitan replaced him with Zhang Xichong, commissioner general of foreign and Han affairs, as Lulong military governor, garrisoning Pingzhou, and sent trusted generals with three hundred horsemen to supervise him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Wenjin defected to the Tang, the Khitan appointed Zhang Xichong—commissioner general over foreign and Han affairs—in his place as military governor of Lulong, with orders to hold Pingzhou under the watch of three hundred Khitan cavalry.

sentences.zh: 希崇本書生，為幽州牙將，沒於契丹，性和易，契丹將稍親信之，因與其部曲謀南歸。

translations.literal: Xichong was originally a literatus and a Ya-jiang of Youzhou; captured by the Khitan, his nature was easygoing, and Khitan generals gradually came to trust him; he therefore plotted with his troops to return south.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong had been a scholar and a staff officer in Youzhou before falling into Khitan hands. Even-tempered and affable, he gradually won the Khitan officers' trust and began plotting with his men to flee south.

sentences.zh: 部曲泣曰：「歸固寢食所不忘也，然虜眾我寡，奈何？」

translations.literal: His troops wept and said: "Returning south is indeed what we never forget even in sleep and at meals, but the barbarians are many and we are few—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: His men wept: "Going home is never far from our thoughts, waking or sleeping—but the enemy outnumber us. What can we do?

sentences.zh: 希崇曰：「吾誘其將殺之，兵必潰去。

translations.literal: Xichong said: "If I lure their generals and kill them, the troops will certainly scatter and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong said: "If I trick their officers into a trap and kill them, their troops will collapse and flee.

sentences.zh: 此去虜帳千餘里，比其知而徵兵，吾屬去遠矣。」

translations.literal: From here to the barbarians' headquarters is more than a thousand li; by the time they learn of it and mobilize troops, our band will be far away."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan capital lies more than a thousand li from here; by the time they learn what happened and muster reinforcements, we will be long gone.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「善！」

translations.literal: The crowd said: "Excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: They all agreed: "Good!

sentences.zh: 乃先為阱，實以石灰，明日，召虜將飲，醉，並從者殺之，投諸阱中。

translations.literal: They then first dug pits and filled them with lime; the next day they invited the barbarian generals to drink; when drunk, they killed them together with their attendants and cast them into the pits.
translations.idiomatic: They dug pits filled with lime, then the next day invited the Khitan officers to a feast; when they were drunk, Xichong's men killed them and their escorts and dumped the bodies into the pits.

sentences.zh: 其營在城北，亟發兵攻之，契丹眾皆潰去。

translations.literal: Their camp was north of the city; he urgently sent troops to attack it, and the Khitan masses all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan garrison lay north of the city; he immediately attacked it, and the Khitan force broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 希崇悉舉其所部二萬餘口來奔，詔以為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Xichong brought his entire following of more than twenty thousand persons in flight to surrender; an edict appointed him prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xichong led more than twenty thousand followers south in a mass defection, and was appointed prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳王太后殂。

translations.literal: The Queen Dowager of Wu died.
translations.idiomatic: The queen dowager of Wu passed away.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛巳，荊南敗楚兵於白田，執楚岳州刺史李廷規，歸於吳。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinsi, Jingnan defeated Chu forces at Baitian, captured Chu prefect of Yuezhou Li Tinggui, and sent him to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinsi, Jingnan routed Chu troops at Baitian, captured Li Tinggui—the Chu prefect of Yuezhou—and delivered him to Wu.

sentences.zh: 乙未，敕以溫韜發諸陵，段凝反覆，令所在賜死。
