translations.literal: On yiwei, an edict ordered that for Wen Tao's opening of the tombs and Duan Ning's repeated betrayals, they were to be granted death wherever located.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei an edict condemned Wen Tao for robbing the imperial tombs and Duan Ning for his repeated treachery, ordering both men executed on sight wherever found.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以武寧節度使房知溫兼荊南行營招討使，知荊南行府事；

translations.literal: On jihai, Wuning military governor Fang Zhiwen was additionally made Jingnan campaign commissioner and put in charge of Jingnan headquarters affairs;
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Fang Zhiwen, military governor of Wuning, was named concurrent Jingnan campaign commissioner and given authority over the Jingnan field headquarters;

sentences.zh: 分遣中使發諸道兵赴襄陽，以討高季興。

translations.literal: Eunuch envoys were separately dispatched to mobilize troops from all circuits to Xiangyang to campaign against Gao Jixing.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch envoys were sent out to every circuit to raise troops for an expedition against Gao Jixing at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，徙慶州防禦使竇廷琬為金州刺史；

translations.literal: On xinchou, Qingzhou defense commissioner Dou Tingwan was transferred to be Jinzhou prefect;
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Dou Tingwan, defense commissioner of Qingzhou, was transferred to the post of Jinzhou prefect;

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，廷琬據慶州拒命。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Tingwan held Qingzhou and refused orders.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, Tingwan seized Qingzhou and defied the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以橫海節度使李從敏兼北面行營副招討使。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Henghai military governor Li Congmin was additionally made deputy northern campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Li Congmin, military governor of Henghai, was appointed deputy northern campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從敏，帝之從子也。

translations.literal: Congmin was the Emperor's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Congmin was the emperor's nephew.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔靜難節度使李敬周發兵討竇廷琬。

translations.literal: On wushen, an edict ordered Jingnan military governor Li Jingzhou to dispatch troops to campaign against Dou Tingwan.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Li Jingzhou, military governor of Jingnan, was ordered to raise an army against Dou Tingwan.

sentences.zh: 王都據定州，守備固，伺察嚴，諸將屢有謀翻城應官軍者，皆不果。

translations.literal: Wang Du held Dingzhou; defenses were solid and surveillance strict; generals repeatedly plotted to turn the city and respond to the imperial army, but none succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du held Dingzhou behind strong defenses and tight surveillance; though several of his officers tried to open the gates to the imperial army, every attempt failed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者促王宴球攻城，晏球與使者聯騎巡城，指之曰：「城高峻如此，借使主人聽外兵登城，亦非梯沖所及。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent an envoy to urge Wang Yanqiu to assault the city; Yanqiu rode side by side with the envoy around the city, pointed to it and said: "The walls are so high and steep; even if the lord of the city allowed outside troops to climb them, they would still be beyond the reach of scaling ladders and siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched an envoy to press Wang Yanqiu for an assault. Yanqiu rode around the walls with the envoy and said: "See how high these walls rise—even if Wang Du were willing to let our men climb them, ladders and battering rams could never reach the top.

sentences.zh: 徒多殺精兵，無損於賊，如此何為！

translations.literal: In vain many crack troops would be killed, without harm to the bandits—what is the use of this!
translations.idiomatic: We would merely slaughter our best soldiers without hurting the rebels in the slightest—what would be the point!

sentences.zh: 不若食三州之租，愛民養兵以俟之，彼必內潰。」

translations.literal: Better to live off the tax grain of the three prefectures, cherish the people and nurture the army while waiting—the enemy is sure to collapse from within."
translations.idiomatic: Better to subsist on the tax revenue of the three nearby prefectures, keep the people safe, and husband our troops until they crack from within.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 十一月，有司請為哀帝位廟，詔立廟於曹州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the relevant offices requested establishing a temple for Emperor Ai; an edict ordered a temple established at Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the ritual authorities petitioned for a temple to Emperor Ai of Tang, and an edict ordered one built at Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使晉忠武公霍彥威卒。

translations.literal: Pinglu military governor Duke of Jin and Marquis of Zhongwu Huo Yanwei died.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei, Duke of Jin and Marquis of Zhongwu, military governor of Pinglu, died.

sentences.zh: 忠州刺史王雅取歸州。

translations.literal: Zhongzhou prefect Wang Ya captured Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, prefect of Zhongzhou, seized Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，皇子從厚納孔循女為妃，循因之得之大梁，厚結王德妃之黨，乞留。

translations.literal: On gengyin, the prince Conghou took Kong Xun's daughter as consort; Xun thereby reached the Great Liang, formed close ties with Consort Wang De's faction, and requested to remain.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Prince Conghou married Kong Xun's daughter. Xun used the connection to reach the capital at Daliang, cultivated allies among Consort Wang De's faction, and asked to stay.

sentences.zh: 安重誨具奏其事，力排之，禮畢，促令歸鎮。

translations.literal: An Chonghui reported the whole affair in detail and forcefully opposed it; when the rites were finished, he urged that Xun be sent back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui reported the whole affair to the throne and argued strenuously against letting Xun remain; once the wedding rites were complete, he pressed for Xun's immediate return to his command.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以中書侍郎、同平章事王建立同平章事，充平盧節度使。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Counselor Wang Jianli was confirmed as Associate Grand Counselor and appointed Pinglu military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Wang Jianli, vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand counselor, was confirmed in his council rank and assigned as military governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 丙申，上問趙鳳：「帝王賜人鐵券，何也？」

translations.literal: On bingshen, the Emperor asked Zhao Feng: "When emperors bestow iron vouchers on people, what is the purpose?"
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the emperor asked Zhao Feng: "What is the purpose of an emperor's iron voucher of immunity?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「與之立誓，令其子孫長享爵祿耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "To establish a vow with them, so that their descendants may long enjoy rank and salary."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng answered: "It is a sworn pledge that the recipient's descendants will forever enjoy rank and emoluments.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「先朝受此賜者讓三人，崇韜、繼麟尋皆族滅，朕得脫如毫釐耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In the previous reign only three received this gift; Chongtao and Jilin soon were both exterminated to the last clan member, and I barely escaped by a hair's breadth."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Only three men received that gift under the previous emperor. Guo Chongtao and Li Jilin were soon executed along with their entire clans, and I myself escaped by a hair's breadth.

sentences.zh: 因歎息久之。

translations.literal: He therefore sighed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He fell silent and sighed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳曰：「帝王心存大信，固不必刻之金石也。」

translations.literal: Zhao Feng said: "When emperors harbor great trust in their hearts, they certainly need not inscribe it on metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng said: "When an emperor's word is truly trustworthy, there is no need to carve it into metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲辰，李敬周奏拔慶州，族竇廷琬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiachen, Li Jingzhou memorialized that Qingzhou had been taken and Dou Tingwan's clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiachen, Li Jingzhou reported the capture of Qingzhou and the execution of Dou Tingwan's entire clan.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使高季興寢疾，命其子行軍司馬、忠義節度使、同平章事從誨權知軍府事；

translations.literal: Jingnan military governor Gao Jixing lay gravely ill and ordered his son, acting military governor, Zhongyi military governor, and Associate Grand Counselor Conghui to exercise provisional control of headquarters affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixing of Jingnan fell seriously ill and entrusted provisional control of the circuit to his son Conghui—acting military governor, military governor of Zhongyi, and associate grand counselor;

sentences.zh: 丙辰，季興卒。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Jixing died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Gao Jixing died.

sentences.zh: 吳主以從誨為荊南節度使兼侍中。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler appointed Conghui Jingnan military governor and concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu appointed Conghui military governor of Jingnan with the concurrent title of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 史館修撰張昭遠上言：「臣竊見先朝時，皇弟、皇子皆喜俳優，入則飾姬妾，出則誇僕馬；

translations.literal: Historiography compiler Zhang Zhaoyuan submitted a memorial: "Your servant has observed that in the former reign, imperial younger brothers and princes all delighted in actors; indoors they adorned concubines, outdoors they boasted of servants and horses;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhaoyuan, compiler at the Historiography Institute, submitted a memorial: "I have noticed that under the previous emperor, princes and imperial brothers all doted on actors—dressing their concubines lavishly at home and showing off their servants and horses abroad;

sentences.zh: 習尚如此，何道能賢！

translations.literal: If custom and fashion are like this, by what Way can they become worthy!
translations.idiomatic: When fashion runs to such pursuits, how can they become virtuous rulers!

sentences.zh: 諸皇子宜精擇師傅，令皇子屈身師事之，講禮義之經，論安危之理。

translations.literal: The various princes ought carefully to select masters, have the princes humble themselves to serve them as teachers, expound the classics of ritual and righteousness, and discuss the principles of security and danger.
translations.idiomatic: Each prince should be given a carefully chosen tutor whom he respects as a true teacher, to instruct him in the classics of ritual and the principles of governance that decide a realm's safety or ruin.

sentences.zh: 古者人君即位則建太子，所以明嫡庶之分，塞禍亂之源。

translations.literal: In antiquity when a ruler assumed the throne he established a crown prince, thereby clarifying the distinction between legitimate and secondary sons and blocking the source of calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity a new emperor would at once name a crown prince, making the line of succession clear and cutting off the roots of succession crises.

sentences.zh: 今卜嗣建儲，臣未敢輕議。

translations.literal: Now in selecting an heir and establishing a storehouse of succession, your servant does not dare speak lightly.
translations.idiomatic: As for choosing an heir and establishing a crown prince today, I do not presume to speak hastily on the matter.

sentences.zh: 至於恩澤賜與之間，婚姻省侍之際，嫡庶長幼，宜有所分，示以等威，絕其僥冀。」

translations.literal: As for occasions of grace, gifts, and bestowals, and at times of marriage and attendance at court, between legitimate and secondary sons, elder and younger, there ought to be distinctions, displaying ranks of dignity and cutting off their vain hopes."
translations.idiomatic: But in the distribution of honors and gifts, and in arrangements for marriage and court attendance, there should be clear distinctions between legitimate and secondary sons, elder and younger—making rank visible and denying them any ground for ambition.

sentences.zh: 帝賞歎其言而不能用。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired and sighed over his words but could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial warmly but did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 閩王延鈞度民二萬為僧，由是閩中多僧。

translations.literal: Min King Yanjun inducted twenty thousand commoners as monks; hence within Min there were many monks.
translations.idiomatic: King Yanjun of Min ordained twenty thousand commoners as monks, and afterward monks were everywhere in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使、北都留守從榮，年少驕很，不親政務，帝遣左右素與從榮善者往與之處，使從容諷導之。

translations.literal: Hedong military governor and northern capital regent Congrong, young, arrogant, and fierce, did not attend to government affairs; the Emperor sent personal attendants who were on good terms with Congrong to stay with him and gently admonish and guide him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congrong, military governor of Hedong and regent at the northern capital, was young, arrogant, and indifferent to governance. The emperor sent attendants who were on friendly terms with him to keep him company and counsel him tactfully.

sentences.zh: 其人私謂從榮曰：「河南相公恭謹好善，親禮端士，有老成之風；

translations.literal: One of them privately told Congrong: "The Henan lord is respectful, cautious, fond of goodness, personally honors upright gentlemen, and has the manner of a seasoned elder;
translations.idiomatic: One of them took Congrong aside and said: "The Prince of Henan is dutiful and upright, treats worthy men with respect, and carries himself with the gravity of a seasoned statesman;

sentences.zh: 相公齒長，宜自策勵，勿令聲問出河南之下。」

translations.literal: Your lordship is older in years; you ought to rouse yourself and not let your reputation fall below Henan's."
translations.idiomatic: You are the elder brother—you should push yourself hard, and not let your standing fall below his.

sentences.zh: 從榮不悅，退，告步軍都指揮使楊思權曰：「朝廷之人皆推從厚而短我，我其廢乎！」

translations.literal: Congrong was displeased; he withdrew and told infantry commander Yang Siquan: "People at court all praise Conghou and speak ill of me—am I to be discarded!"
translations.idiomatic: Congrong bristled at this. Afterwards he told Yang Siquan, commander of the infantry guard: "Everyone at court favors Conghou and belittles me. Am I being passed over for succession?

sentences.zh: 思權曰：「相公手握強兵，且有思權在，何憂？」

translations.literal: Siquan said: "Your lordship holds strong troops in hand, and with Siquan here, what worry is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Siquan replied: "You command a powerful army, and I am here beside you—what is there to worry about?

sentences.zh: 因勸從榮多募部曲，繕甲兵，陰為自固之備。

translations.literal: He therefore urged Congrong to recruit many retainers, repair armor and weapons, and secretly prepare to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Congrong to recruit more retainers, stockpile arms and armor, and quietly build up his own strength.

sentences.zh: 又謂帝左右曰：「君每譽弟而抑其兄，我輩豈不能助之邪！」

translations.literal: He also told the Emperor's attendants: "You daily praise the younger brother and suppress the elder—can we not assist him!"
translations.idiomatic: He also warned the emperor's attendants: "You keep praising the younger son while running down the elder—do you think we cannot support our lord?

sentences.zh: 其人懼，以告副留守馮贇，贇密奏之。

translations.literal: That man was afraid and reported it to deputy regent Feng Yun; Yun secretly memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant was alarmed and reported Yang's words to deputy regent Feng Yun, who submitted a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝召思權詣闕，以從榮故，亦弗之罪也。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Siquan to court; on account of Congrong, he also did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yang Siquan to the capital but, for Congrong's sake, did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝中之上天成四年（

translations.literal: Middle section of Emperor Mingzong the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Filially Pious—upper part, Tiancheng year 4 (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong the Sagely, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Filially Pious—middle section, upper part: Tiancheng year 4 (

sentences.zh: 己丑，公元九二九年）

translations.literal: jichou, CE 929)
translations.idiomatic: jichou, 929 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，馮贇入為宣徽使，謂執政曰：「從榮剛僻而輕易，宜選重德輔之。」

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Feng Yun entered the capital as Director of the Palace Secretariat and told the chief ministers: "Congrong is obstinate, perverse, and rash; a man of weighty virtue ought to be chosen to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Feng Yun arrived at court as director of the palace secretariat and told the chief ministers: "Congrong is headstrong and reckless; he needs a sober, experienced mentor at his side.

sentences.zh: 王都、禿餒欲突圍走，不得出。

translations.literal: Wang Du and Tueri wished to break out and flee but could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Du and the Khitan general Tueri tried to break out of the siege but could not escape.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸丑，定州都指揮使馬讓能開門納官軍，都舉族自焚，擒禿餒及契丹二千人。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guichou, Dingzhou chief commander Ma Rangneng opened the gate and admitted the imperial army; Du's entire clan burned themselves to death; Tueri and two thousand Khitan were captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guichou, Ma Rangneng, chief commander of Dingzhou, opened the gates to the imperial army. Wang Du and his family set themselves on fire; Tueri and two thousand Khitan troops were taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以王晏球為天平節度使，與趙德鈞並加兼侍中。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Wang Yanqiu was made Tianping military governor, and together with Zhao Dejun both were additionally granted concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Wang Yanqiu was appointed military governor of Tianping, and both he and Zhao Dejun were promoted to the concurrent rank of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 禿餒至大梁，斬於市。

translations.literal: Tueri reached the Great Liang and was beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Tueri was taken to Daliang and executed in the public square.

sentences.zh: 樞密使趙敬怡卒。

translations.literal: Commissioner of Military Affairs Zhao Jingyi died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jingyi, commissioner of military affairs, died.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝發大梁。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Emperor departed the Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor left Daliang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，門下侍郎、同平章事崔協卒於須水。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Grand Counselor Cui Xie died at Xushui.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Cui Xie, vice director of the chancellery and associate grand counselor, died at Xushui.

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝至洛陽。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Emperor reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor arrived in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 王宴球在定州城下，日以私財饗士，自始攻至克城未嘗戮一卒。

translations.literal: Wang Yanqiu was below the walls of Dingzhou; daily he treated the troops with his private wealth; from the beginning of the assault until the capture of the city he never once executed a single soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the siege of Dingzhou, Wang Yanqiu feasted his troops daily at his own expense, and from the first day of the assault until the city fell he never once put a soldier to death.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛巳，晏球入朝，帝美其功；

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinsi, Yanqiu entered court audience; the Emperor praised his achievement;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinsi, Yanqiu returned to court, and the emperor commended his victory;

sentences.zh: 晏球謝久煩饋運而已。

translations.literal: Yanqiu thanked them only for the long trouble of supplying transport.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu merely apologized for having been such a burden on the supply lines for so long.

sentences.zh: 皇子右衛大將軍從璨性剛，安重誨用事，從璨不為之屈。

translations.literal: The prince, General of the Right Guard Congcan, was by nature stern; An Chonghui wielded power, and Congcan would not yield to him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Congcan, general of the right guard, had a stubborn temper; though An Chonghui dominated the court, Congcan refused to defer to him.

sentences.zh: 帝東巡，以從璨為皇城使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured east, he made Congcan commissioner of the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's eastern tour, Congcan was appointed commissioner of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 從璨與客宴於會節園，酒酣，戲登御榻，重誨奏請誅之；

translations.literal: Congcan feasted with guests in the Festival Garden; when wine was deep, he playfully mounted the imperial couch; Chonghui memorialized requesting his execution;
translations.idiomatic: Congcan hosted a banquet for guests in the Festival Garden; drunk, he climbed onto the imperial couch in jest. An Chonghui memorialized demanding his execution;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，賜從璨死。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Congcan was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Congcan was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 橫山蠻寇邵州。

translations.literal: Hengshan barbarians raided Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hengshan tribesmen raided Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷命其子武安節度副使、判長沙府希聲知政事，總錄內外諸軍事，自是國政先歷希聲，乃聞於殷。

translations.literal: Chu King Yin ordered his son, Wuan deputy military governor and administrator of Changsha Prefecture Xisheng, to manage government affairs and supervise all internal and external military affairs; from this the state's government first passed through Xisheng before reaching Yin.
translations.idiomatic: King Yin of Chu put his son Xisheng—deputy military governor of Wuan and administrator of Changsha—in charge of civil administration and all military affairs, so that from then on state business went to Xisheng first and only then reached the king.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子朔，禁鐵錫錢。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of gengzi, iron and tin coin were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of gengzi, iron and tin coinage was banned.

sentences.zh: 時湖南專用錫錢，銅錢一直錫錢百，流入中國，法不能禁。

translations.literal: At that time Hunan used only tin coin; one copper cash equaled one hundred tin cash; they flowed into the central realm and the law could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan used almost nothing but tin coins, worth one copper coin to every hundred tin; they flooded into the central provinces, and the ban proved impossible to enforce.

sentences.zh: 丙午，楚六軍副使王環敗荊南兵於石首。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Chu Six Armies deputy commissioner Wang Huan defeated Jingnan troops at Shishou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Wang Huan, deputy commissioner of the Chu Six Armies, routed Jingnan forces at Shishou.

sentences.zh: 初令緣邊置場市党項馬，不令詣闕。

translations.literal: An initial order directed that along the frontier markets be established for Tangut horses, and that they not be allowed to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: A new rule established frontier markets for Tangut horses and forbade them from being brought to the capital as tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，党項皆詣闕，以貢馬為名，國家約其直酬之，加以館谷賜與，歲費五十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: Previously, Tangut all came to court in the name of offering tribute horses; the state paid them the appraised value, and in addition provided lodging, grain, and gifts, costing more than five hundred thousand strings per year.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Tangut tribesmen had come to court bearing horses as "tribute"; the state paid market price for each mount, then housed and fed the envoys and showered them with gifts—costing the treasury more than five hundred thousand strings of cash a year.

sentences.zh: 有司苦其耗蠹，故止之。

translations.literal: The relevant offices were distressed by this drain and waste, and therefore stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The fiscal authorities had long complained of the expense, which is why the practice was halted.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以皇子從榮為河南尹、判六軍諸衛事，從厚為河東節度使、北都留守。

translations.literal: On renzi, the imperial prince Congrong was made metropolitan prefect of Henan and given charge of the Six Armies and the various palace guards; Conghou was made military governor of Hedong and regent of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the prince Congrong was appointed Metropolitan Prefect of Henan and placed in charge of the Six Armies and palace guards, while Conghou was made military governor of Hedong and regent of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇雲州。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan forces raided Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以端明殿學士、兵部侍郎趙鳳為門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Duanming Hall academician and vice-minister of war Zhao Feng was made vice minister of the Secretariat and co-director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Zhao Feng, Duanming Hall academician and Vice Minister of War, was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙酉，中書言：「太常改謚哀帝日昭宣光烈孝皇帝，廟號景宗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yiyou, the Secretariat said: "The Court of Imperial Sacrifices changed the posthumous title of Emperor Ai to Zhao Xuan Guanglie Xiao Huangdi and gave him the temple name Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yiyou, the Secretariat reported: "The Court of Imperial Sacrifices has posthumously titled Emperor Ai as the Bright, Propagating, Glorious, Filially Pious Emperor and assigned him the temple name Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 既稱宗則應入太廟，在別廟則不應稱宗。」

translations.literal: If called 'zong' then one ought to enter the Grand Temple; if in a separate temple then one ought not be called 'zong'."
translations.idiomatic: A ruler styled 'zong' belongs in the Grand Temple; if he is housed in a separate shrine, he should not bear that designation."

sentences.zh: 乃去廟號。

translations.literal: Thereupon the temple name was removed.
translations.idiomatic: The temple name was accordingly dropped.

sentences.zh: 帝將祀南郊，遣客省使李仁矩以詔諭兩川，今西川獻錢一百萬緡，東川五十萬緡；

translations.literal: The emperor was about to sacrifice at the Southern Suburb; he sent reception commissioner Li Renju with an edict to inform the Two Shu circuits, ordering Western Shu to contribute one million strings and Eastern Shu five hundred thousand strings;
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to offer sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, he dispatched Reception Commissioner Li Renju with an edict to the Two Shu circuits, demanding one million strings of cash from Western Shu and half a million from Eastern Shu;

sentences.zh: 皆辭以軍用不足，西川獻五十萬緡，東川獻十萬緡。

translations.literal: All pleaded insufficient military funds; Western Shu contributed five hundred thousand strings, Eastern Shu one hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Both circuits pleaded insufficient military funds; Western Shu sent only five hundred thousand strings and Eastern Shu only one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 仁矩，帝在籓鎮時客將也，為安重誨所厚，恃恩驕慢。

translations.literal: Renju had been a guest general when the emperor was at a frontier command; favored by An Chonghui, he relied on that grace and was arrogant and rude.
translations.idiomatic: Renju had served as a client general when the emperor held a frontier command; An Chonghui favored him, and he grew arrogant on that patronage.

sentences.zh: 至梓州，董璋置宴召之，日中不往，方擁妓酣飲。

translations.literal: When he reached Zizhou, Dong Zhang set a banquet and summoned him; at midday he did not go, but was instead embracing courtesans and drinking freely.
translations.idiomatic: At Zizhou, Dong Zhang laid a banquet and summoned him, but at midday Renju still had not appeared—he was in his quarters, courtesans in his arms, drinking his fill.

sentences.zh: 璋怒，從卒徒執兵入驛，立仁矩於階下而詬之曰：「公但聞西川斬李客省，謂我獨不能邪！」

translations.literal: Zhang was angry; with attendant soldiers and guards bearing weapons they entered the post station, stood Renju below the steps, and reviled him, saying: "Your Lordship has only heard that Western Shu executed Commissioner Li of the Reception Office—do you think I alone cannot do the same!"
translations.idiomatic: In a rage Zhang sent armed retainers into the post station, thrust Renju down the steps, and berated him: "You've heard how Western Shu beheaded the Reception Commissioner named Li—do you think I'm incapable of the same!"

sentences.zh: 仁矩流涕拜請，僅而得免；

translations.literal: Renju wept, prostrated himself in plea, and barely escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Renju wept and begged on his knees and barely escaped with his life;

sentences.zh: 既而厚賂仁矩以謝之。

translations.literal: Afterward he lavishly bribed Renju to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he paid Renju a heavy bribe by way of apology.

sentences.zh: 仁矩還，言璋不法。

translations.literal: Renju returned and reported Zhang's lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court Renju denounced Zhang's defiance of the law.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝復遣退事舍人李彥珣詣東川，入境，失小禮，璋拘其從者，彥珣奔還。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor again sent palace attendant Li Yanxun to Eastern Shu; upon entering the circuit he committed a minor breach of etiquette; Zhang detained his attendants and Yanxun fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after the emperor sent palace attendant Li Yanxun to Eastern Shu again; Yanxun committed some small breach of protocol on crossing the border, Zhang seized his escort, and Yanxun fled home.

sentences.zh: 高季興之叛也，其子從誨節諫，不聽。

translations.literal: When Gao Jixing rebelled, his son Conghui admonished him in restraint; he did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jixing rebelled, his son Conghui cautioned restraint, but Jixing would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 從誨既襲位，謂僚佐曰：「唐近而吳遠，捨近臣遠，非計也。」

translations.literal: After Conghui succeeded to the position, he told his staff: "Tang is near and Wu is far; to abandon the near and serve the far is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: Once Conghui had succeeded him, he told his advisers: "Tang is close and Wu is distant—to abandon a near patron for a far one is folly."

sentences.zh: 乃因楚王殷以謝罪於唐。

translations.literal: Thereupon by means of King Yin of Chu he submitted an apology to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He then made his peace with Tang through King Yin of Chu.

sentences.zh: 又遺山南東道節度使安元信書，求保奏，復修職貢。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Shannan East Circuit military governor An Yuanxin, asking him to guarantee a memorial and restore tribute duties and offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Shannan East Circuit military governor An Yuanxin, asking him to intercede and restore the circuit's tribute obligations.

sentences.zh: 丙申，元信以從誨書聞，帝許之。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Yuanxin reported Conghui's letter, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Yuanxin forwarded Conghui's letter and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇雲州。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan forces raided Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊申，復以鄴都為魏州，留守、皇城使並停。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wushen, Yedu was again made Wei Prefecture; the regent and palace-city commissioner posts were both abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wushen, Yedu was once again designated Wei Prefecture, and the posts of regent and palace-city commissioner were abolished.

sentences.zh: 庚申，高從誨自稱前荊南行軍司馬、歸州刺史，上表求內附。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Gao Conghui styled himself former Jingnan expeditionary deputy commissioner and prefect of Gui, and submitted a memorial seeking internal attachment.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Gao Conghui submitted a memorial seeking to rejoin the empire, styling himself former Jingnan expeditionary deputy commissioner and prefect of Gui.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲申，以從誨為荊南節度使兼侍中。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiashen, Conghui was made military governor of Jingnan and concurrently chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiashen Conghui was appointed military governor of Jingnan and Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 己丑，罷荊南招討使。

translations.literal: On jichou, the Jingnan pacification commissioner was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Jingnan pacification commissioner post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 八月，吳武昌節度使兼侍中李簡以疾求還江都，癸丑，卒於採石。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wu Wuchang military governor and concurrent chief minister Li Jian, on account of illness, sought to return to Jiangdu; on guichou he died at Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Li Jian, Wu's military governor of Wuchang and Grand Counselor, asked to return to Jiangdu on account of illness; on guichou he died at Caishi.

sentences.zh: 徐知詢，簡婿也，擅留簡親兵二千人於金陵，表薦簡子彥忠代父鎮鄂州，徐知誥以龍武統軍柴再用為武昌節度使；

translations.literal: Xu Zhixun, Jian's son-in-law, on his own authority retained two thousand of Jian's personal troops at Jinling, and memorialized recommending Jian's son Yanzhong to replace his father in governing Ezhou; Xu Zhigao appointed Dragon Martial commanding general Chai Zaiyong as Wuchang military governor;
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son-in-law Xu Zhixun kept two thousand of his father-in-law's personal troops at Jinling and recommended Jian's son Yanzhong to succeed him at Ezhou; Xu Zhigao instead installed Dragon Martial commanding general Chai Zaiyong as military governor of Wuchang;

sentences.zh: 知詢怒曰：「劉崇俊，兄之親，三世為濠州；

translations.literal: Zhixun said angrily: "Liu Chongjun is our elder brother's kinsman—three generations as prefect of Hao;
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun fumed: "Liu Chongjun is kin to our elder brother—his family held Haozhou for three generations;

sentences.zh: 彥忠吾妻族，獨不得邪！」

translations.literal: Yanzhong is my wife's kin—is he alone not permitted!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhong is my wife's kin—why should he alone be denied!"

sentences.zh: 初，楚王殷用都軍判官高郁為謀主，國賴以富強，鄰國皆疾之。

translations.literal: Initially King Yin of Chu used chief army judge Gao Yu as his chief strategist; the state relied on him to grow rich and strong, and all neighboring states envied this.
translations.idiomatic: Early on King Yin of Chu had relied on chief army judge Gao Yu as his chief strategist; under Yu's counsel the state grew prosperous and strong, to every neighbor's resentment.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入洛，殷貴其子希範入貢，莊宗愛其警敏，曰：「比聞馬氏當為高郁所奪，今有子如此，郁安能得之！」

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Yin prized his son Xifan for going to offer tribute; Zhuangzong loved his quick wit and said: "I lately heard the Ma house would be seized by Gao Yu—with a son like this, how could Yu obtain it!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Yin had sent his son Xifan as tribute envoy; the emperor was taken with the boy's quick mind and said, "People said the Ma clan would fall to Gao Yu—with an heir like this, Yu hasn't a chance!"

sentences.zh: 高季興亦以流言間鬱於殷，殷不聽；

translations.literal: Gao Jixing also used slander to drive a wedge between Yu and Yin; Yin did not listen;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixing also tried to turn Yin against Yu with rumors, but Yin would not listen;

sentences.zh: 乃遣使遺節度副使、知政事希聲書，盛稱郁功名，願為兄弟。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent an envoy with a letter to deputy military governor and director of governance Xisheng, lavishly praising Yu's achievements and desiring to become brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he sent an envoy to deputy military governor and chief minister Xisheng with a letter lavishing praise on Yu's achievements and offering brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 使者言於希聲曰：「高公常云『馬氏政事皆出高郁』，此子孫之憂也。」

translations.literal: The envoy said to Xisheng: "Lord Gao often says 'All Ma house governance comes from Gao Yu'—this is anxiety for descendants."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy told Xisheng: "Lord Gao often says, 'The Ma family's affairs all run through Gao Yu'—a dangerous thing for their heirs."

sentences.zh: 希聲信之。

translations.literal: Xisheng believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheng believed him.

sentences.zh: 行軍司馬楊昭遂，希聲之妻族也，謀代郁任，日譖之於希聲。

translations.literal: Expeditionary deputy commissioner Yang Zhaosui, Xisheng's wife's kin, plotted to replace Yu in office and daily slandered him to Xisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Expeditionary deputy commissioner Yang Zhaosui, a kinsman of Xisheng's wife, schemed to take Yu's place and daily poisoned Xisheng's ears against him.

sentences.zh: 希聲屢言於殷，稱郁奢僭，且外交鄰籓，請誅之。

translations.literal: Xisheng repeatedly spoke to Yin, calling Yu extravagant and presumptuous, and moreover maintaining ties with neighboring circuits, and asked to have him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheng repeatedly urged Yin that Yu was arrogant and overreaching, consorting with neighboring circuits, and ought to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 殷曰：「成吾功業，皆郁力也；

translations.literal: Yin said: "Accomplishing my achievements—all is Yu's strength;
translations.idiomatic: Yin replied: "Everything I've built, Yu made possible;

sentences.zh: 汝勿為此言！」

translations.literal: You must not speak this way!"
translations.idiomatic: Don't you say such things again!"

sentences.zh: 希聲固請罷其兵柄，乃左遷郁行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Xisheng insisted on requesting removal of his military authority; thereupon Yu was demoted to expeditionary deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xisheng kept pressing to strip Yu of military command, Yin demoted Yu to expeditionary deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 郁謂所親曰：「亟營西山，吾將歸老。

translations.literal: Yu told those close to him: "Quickly prepare West Mountain—I will retire there in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu told his intimates: "Start building my retreat on West Mountain—I'm going to retire.

sentences.zh: 猘子漸大，能咋人矣。」

translations.literal: The whelp is gradually growing; it can bite people now."
translations.idiomatic: The pup is growing teeth—it can bite now."

sentences.zh: 希聲聞之，益怒，明日，矯以殷命殺鬱於府捨，榜諭中外，誣郁謀叛，並誅其族黨。

translations.literal: When Xisheng heard this he grew angrier still; the next day, falsely using Yin's command, he killed Yu at the headquarters lodging, posted proclamations throughout court and realm, falsely accusing Yu of plotting rebellion, and also executed his clan and associates.
translations.idiomatic: When Xisheng heard that he flew into a worse rage; the next day he forged the king's order, killed Yu at headquarters, posted notices throughout the realm accusing Yu of treason, and had his kin and followers executed as well.

sentences.zh: 至暮，殷尚未知，是日，大霧，殷謂左右曰：「吾昔從孫儒渡淮，每殺不辜，多致茲異。

translations.literal: By evening Yin still did not know; that day there was heavy fog; Yin told those at his side: "I formerly followed Sun Ru in crossing the Huai; each time we killed the innocent, this sort of marvel often resulted.
translations.idiomatic: By evening Yin still knew nothing; a heavy fog settled that day, and Yin told his attendants: "When I followed Sun Ru across the Huai, innocent blood we spilled always brought omens like this.

sentences.zh: 馬步院豈有冤死者乎？」

translations.literal: Could there be one wrongfully killed in the Horse and Foot yard?"
translations.idiomatic: Has someone been wrongly killed in the Horse and Foot yard?"

sentences.zh: 明日，吏以郁死告，殷拊膺大慟曰：「吾老耄，政非己出，使我勳舊橫罹冤酷！」

translations.literal: The next day an official reported Yu's death; Yin beat his breast and wailed greatly, saying: "I am old and senile; governance is not in my own hands—it has made my meritorious elders suffer wrongful cruelty!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day an official reported Yu's death. Yin clutched his chest and wept: "I'm old and feeble, no longer master of my own court—and now a veteran of my service dies in injustice!"

sentences.zh: 既而顧左右曰：「吾亦何可久處此乎！」

translations.literal: Then turning to those at his side he said: "How can I long remain here!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he looked around and said: "How much longer can I stay in this place!"

sentences.zh: 九月，上與馮道從容語及年谷屢登，四方無事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the emperor conversed at ease with Feng Dao and spoke of successive good harvests and peace on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor spoke easily with Feng Dao of bumper harvests year after year and quiet on every frontier.

sentences.zh: 道曰：「臣常記昔在先皇幕府，奉使中山，歷井陘之險，臣憂馬蹶，執轡甚謹，幸而無失；

translations.literal: Dao said: "Your servant often recalls when in the late emperor's staff I was sent on mission to Zhongshan, traversing the peril of Jingxing Pass; your servant feared the horse would stumble and held the reins very carefully, fortunately without mishap;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said: "I still remember serving in the late emperor's staff, when I was sent to Zhongshan and rode the treacherous Jingxing Pass—I gripped the reins for fear of a stumble and came through safely;

sentences.zh: 逮至平路，放轡自逸，俄至顛隕。

translations.literal: When I reached level road I loosened the reins and let myself relax, and soon I fell and was injured.
translations.idiomatic: Then on level ground I let the reins slack and relaxed—and promptly fell.

sentences.zh: 凡為天下者亦猶是也。」

translations.literal: In all matters, ruling the realm is also like this."
translations.idiomatic: Governing an empire is no different."

sentences.zh: 上深以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point to heart.

sentences.zh: 上又問道：「今歲雖豐，百姓贍足否？」

translations.literal: The emperor again asked Dao: "Though this year is abundant, are the common people sufficiently provisioned?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again: "Harvests are good this year—are the people actually getting by?"

sentences.zh: 道曰：「農家歲凶則死於流殍，歲豐則傷於谷賤，豐凶皆病者，惟農家為然。

translations.literal: Dao said: "Farm households in bad years die amid wandering starvation; in good years they are hurt by cheap grain—both abundance and famine bring illness, and only farm households are so.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao replied: "In famine years farmers starve to death on the roads; in bumper years they're ruined by cheap grain—misery comes in both plenty and want, and farmers alone know it.

sentences.zh: 臣記進士聶夷中詩云：『二月賣新絲，五月糶新谷；

translations.literal: Your servant recalls the poem of jinshi Nie Yizhong: 'In the second month sell new silk, in the fifth month sell new grain;
translations.idiomatic: I remember a poem by the jinshi Nie Yizhong: 'In the second month they sell fresh silk; in the fifth month they sell the new grain;

sentences.zh: 醫得眼下瘡，剜卻心頭肉。』

translations.literal: Curing the sore before the eyes, gouging out the flesh of the heart.'
translations.idiomatic: To heal the wound before their eyes they cut out the flesh of their hearts.'

sentences.zh: 語雖鄙俚，曲盡田家之情狀。

translations.literal: Though the words are vulgar and common, they exhaustively portray the condition of farm families.
translations.idiomatic: The lines are coarse, but they capture peasant life exactly.

sentences.zh: 農於四人之中最為勤苦，人主不可不知也。」

translations.literal: Among the four classes of people, farmers are the most toiling and bitter; a ruler must not fail to know this."
translations.idiomatic: Of the four estates farmers toil hardest—a ruler must never forget that."

sentences.zh: 上悅，命左右錄其詩，常諷誦之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased; he ordered attendants to copy the poem and often recited it to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor had the poem copied and often chanted it aloud.

sentences.zh: 鄜州兵戍東川者歸本道，董璋擅留其壯者，選贏老歸之，仍收其甲兵。

translations.literal: Fu Prefecture troops garrisoning Eastern Shu returned to their circuit; Dong Zhang on his own authority retained the strong ones, selected the weak and old to send back, and moreover confiscated their armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Prefecture troops finishing garrison duty in Eastern Shu were sent home, but Dong Zhang kept the able-bodied men, returned only the weak and aged, and seized their arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，西川右都押牙孟容弟為資州稅官，坐自盜抵死，觀察判官馮璩、中門副使王處回為之請，孟知祥曰：「雖吾弟犯法，亦不可貸，況他人乎！」

translations.literal: On guisi, Western Shu right chief military adjutant Meng Rong's younger brother served as Zizhou tax official; convicted of embezzling on his own account he was sentenced to death; observation judge Feng Qi and inner-gate deputy commissioner Wang Chuhui pleaded for him; Meng Zhixiang said: "Though my younger brother violated the law, he still cannot be pardoned—how much more so others!"
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the younger brother of Western Shu's right chief military adjutant Meng Rong, a tax official at Zizhou, was sentenced to death for embezzlement; observation judge Feng Qi and inner-gate deputy Wang Chuhui interceded for him, but Meng Zhixiang said: "Even though he is my brother, the law stands—how much less should anyone else expect mercy!"

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐居其國好自大，朝廷使者曲意奉之則贈遺豐厚，不然則禮遇疏薄。

translations.literal: Wuyue king Qian Liu in his state loved to arrogate greatness to himself; if court envoys curried favor he gave rich gifts, otherwise his courtesy was sparse and thin.
translations.idiomatic: In his own realm King Qian Liu of Wuyue liked to play the sovereign; envoys who flattered him received lavish gifts, while those who did not were treated with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 嘗遺安重誨書，辭禮頗倨。

translations.literal: Once he sent a letter to An Chonghui; the wording and courtesy were quite haughty.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote An Chonghui a letter whose tone and formality were brazenly superior.

sentences.zh: 帝遣供奉官烏昭遇、韓玫使吳越，昭遇與玫有隙，使還，玫奏：「昭遇見鏐，稱臣拜舞，謂鏐為殿下，及私以國事告鏐。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent tribute commissioners Wu Zhaoyu and Han Mei as envoys to Wuyue; Zhaoyu and Mei had a rift; when the mission returned Mei memorialized: "When Zhaoyu saw Liu he called himself subject and performed obeisance, addressed Liu as Your Highness, and privately told Liu state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent tribute commissioners Wu Zhaoyu and Han Mei to Wuyue; the two were at odds, and on their return Mei accused Zhaoyu of prostrating himself before Liu as a subject, addressing him as "Your Highness," and leaking state secrets."

sentences.zh: 安重誨奏賜昭遇死。

translations.literal: An Chonghui memorialized to grant Zhaoyu death.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui urged that Zhaoyu be executed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，制鏐以太師致仕，自餘官爵皆削之，凡吳越進奏官、使者、綱吏，令所在系治之。

translations.literal: On guisi, Liu was ordered to retire as Grand Preceptor; all other titles and ranks were stripped; all Wuyue memorial envoys, envoys, and transport clerks were ordered to be detained wherever found.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Liu was forced to retire as Grand Preceptor and stripped of every other title; Wuyue memorial officers, envoys, and transport agents were to be arrested wherever found.

sentences.zh: 鏐令子傳瓘等上表訟冤，皆不省。

translations.literal: Liu had his sons Chuanguan and others submit memorials pleading injustice; none were heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu had his sons Chuanguan and others petition for redress, but the court ignored them.

sentences.zh: 初，朔方節度使韓洙卒，弟澄為留後。

translations.literal: Initially Shuofang military governor Han Zhu died, and his younger brother Cheng became acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang military governor Han Zhu had died, leaving his brother Cheng as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，定遠軍使李匡賓聚黨據保靜鎮作亂，朔方不安；

translations.literal: Before long, Dingyuan army commissioner Li Kuangbin gathered a faction, seized Baojing Town and rebelled; Shuofang was unsettled;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Dingyuan army commissioner Li Kuangbin raised a faction, seized Baojing Town, and rebelled, leaving Shuofang in turmoil;

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，韓澄遣使繼絹表乞朝廷命帥。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou, Han Cheng sent envoys with successive silks and memorial begging the court to appoint a commander.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingyou Han Cheng sent envoys bearing tribute silk and a memorial pleading for a court-appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 前磁州刺史康福，善胡語，上退朝，多召入便殿，訪以時事，福以胡語對；

translations.literal: Former Cizhou prefect Kang Fu was skilled in barbarian tongues; after the emperor left court he often summoned Fu into the privy chamber to inquire about current affairs, and Fu answered in barbarian tongue;
translations.idiomatic: Former prefect of Cizhou Kang Fu spoke the northern tongues; after audiences the emperor often brought him into the privy chamber to discuss affairs of the day, and Fu answered in those languages;

sentences.zh: 安重誨惡之，常戒之曰：「康福，汝但妄奏事，會當斬汝！」

translations.literal: An Chonghui hated this and often warned him: "Kang Fu, you need only falsely memorialize affairs and you'll surely be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui hated this and repeatedly warned him: "Kang Fu, keep fabricating reports to the throne and I'll have your head!"

sentences.zh: 福懼，求外補。

translations.literal: Fu feared this and sought an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Fu asked for a provincial appointment.

sentences.zh: 重誨以靈州深入胡境，為帥者多遇害，戊戌，以福為朔方、河西節度使。

translations.literal: Chonghui considered that Ling Prefecture lay deep in barbarian territory and commanders were often killed; on wuxu Fu was made military governor of Shuofang and Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui noted that Lingzhou lay deep in barbarian country and its governors often met violent ends; on wuxu he had Fu appointed military governor of Shuofang and Hexi.

sentences.zh: 福見上，涕泣辭之；

translations.literal: Fu saw the emperor and weeping declined the post;
translations.idiomatic: When Fu presented himself he wept and begged to be excused;

sentences.zh: 上命重誨為福更他鎮，重誨曰：「福自刺史無功建節，尚復何求！

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chonghui to change Fu to another command; Chonghui said: "Fu rose from prefect without merit to receive a commission—what more does he seek!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told An Chonghui to give Fu another circuit, but Chonghui said: "Fu went from prefect to commissioner with no achievements to his name—what more does he want!

sentences.zh: 且成命已行，難以復改。」

translations.literal: Moreover the completed appointment has already been issued; it is hard to change again."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the appointment is already published—it cannot be undone."

sentences.zh: 上不得已，謂福曰：「重誨不肯，非朕意也。」

translations.literal: The emperor had no alternative; he told Fu: "Chonghui will not agree—this is not my intent."
translations.idiomatic: With no choice the emperor told Fu: "Chonghui wouldn't bend—this isn't what I wanted for you."

sentences.zh: 福辭行，上遣將軍牛知柔、河中都指揮使衛審𡷣等將兵萬人衛送之。

translations.literal: Fu took leave to depart; the emperor sent general Niu Zhirou, Hezhong capital guard commander Wei Shenjun, and others to lead ten thousand troops to escort and deliver him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu set out; the emperor dispatched general Niu Zhirou and Hezhong guard commander Wei Shenjun with ten thousand men to escort him safely.

sentences.zh: 審𡷣，徐州人也。

translations.literal: Shenjun was a man of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shenjun was a native of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，割閬、果二州置保寧軍，壬子，以內客省使李仁矩為節度使。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Lang and Guo two prefectures were carved out to establish Baoning Army; on renzi, inner reception commissioner Li Renju was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Lang and Guo prefectures were split off to form the Baoning Army circuit; on renzi Inner Reception Commissioner Li Renju was appointed its military governor.

sentences.zh: 先是，西川常發芻糧饋峽路，孟知祥辭以本道兵自多，難以奉它鎮，詔不許，屢督之；

translations.literal: Previously Western Shu regularly sent fodder and grain to supply the Gorges route; Meng Zhixiang declined on the grounds that this circuit's troops were already numerous and could hardly supply other commands; the edict did not permit this, and repeatedly pressed him;
translations.idiomatic: Western Shu had long sent fodder and grain to supply the Three Gorges garrison, but Meng Zhixiang pleaded that his own circuit's armies left him no margin to feed other commands; the court refused and kept pressing him;

sentences.zh: 甲寅，知祥奏稱財力乏，不奉詔。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Zhixiang memorialized claiming financial strength was exhausted and would not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Meng Zhixiang memorialized that his treasury was empty and he would defy the order.

sentences.zh: 吳諸道副都統、鎮海寧國節使兼侍中徐知詢自以握兵據上流，意輕徐知誥，數與知誥爭權，內相猜忌，知誥患之，內樞密使王令謀曰：「公輔政日久，挾天子以令境內，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: Wu circuits deputy overall commander, Zhenhai and Ningguo military governor and concurrent chief minister Xu Zhixun, considering himself to hold troops and occupy the upper reaches, looked lightly on Xu Zhigao and repeatedly vied for power with Zhigao; internally they were mutually suspicious; Zhigao worried about this; inner privy councilor Wang Lingmou said: "Your Lordship has assisted governance for long; holding the Son of Heaven you command within the realm—who dares not obey!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhixun of Wu, deputy overall commander of all circuits and military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo as well as Grand Counselor, considered himself strong because he held troops on the upper Yangtze and looked down on Xu Zhigao; the two repeatedly clashed for power, each wary of the other. Zhigao was troubled; inner privy councilor Wang Lingmou told him: "You've governed for years—who in the realm dares defy a regent who holds the throne!

sentences.zh: 知詢年少，恩信未洽於人，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Zhixun is young; grace and trust have not yet reached the people—he can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun is young and hasn't won men's loyalty—he cannot stand against you."

sentences.zh: 知詢待諸弟薄，諸弟皆怨之。

translations.literal: Zhixun treated his younger brothers harshly; all the younger brothers resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun treated his younger brothers harshly and they all resented him.

sentences.zh: 徐玠知知詢不可輔，反持其短以附知誥。

translations.literal: Xu Jie knew Zhixun could not be assisted and instead seized on his faults to attach himself to Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie saw that Zhixun was a lost cause and instead fed Zhigao every fault he could find.

sentences.zh: 吳越王鏐遺知詢金玉鞍勒、器皿，皆飾以龍鳳；

translations.literal: Wuyue king Qian Liu sent Zhixun gold and jade saddle fittings and vessels, all ornamented with dragons and phoenixes;
translations.idiomatic: King Qian Liu of Wuyue sent Zhixun golden and jade saddle fittings and vessels all emblazoned with dragons and phoenixes;

sentences.zh: 知詢不以為嫌，乘用之。

translations.literal: Zhixun did not consider this taboo and rode and used them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun saw no impropriety in gifts fit for a sovereign and used them openly.

sentences.zh: 知詢典客周廷望說知詢曰：「公誠能捐寶華以結朝中勳舊，使皆歸心於公，則彼誰與處！」

translations.literal: Zhixun's chief of guests Zhou Tingwang persuaded Zhixun: "If Your Lordship can truly spend treasures to bind the court's meritorious elders so that all turn their hearts to you, then with whom will he stand!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun's master of guests Zhou Tingwang urged him: "If you lavish gifts on the court's veteran ministers and win their loyalty, who will stand with him then!"

sentences.zh: 知詢從之，使廷望如江都諭意。

translations.literal: Zhixun followed this; he sent Tingwang to Jiangdu to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun agreed and sent Tingwang to Jiangdu to make his approach.

sentences.zh: 廷望與知誥親吏周宗善，密輸款於知誥，亦以知誥陰謀告知詢。

translations.literal: Tingwang was on good terms with Zhigao's personal clerk Zhou Zong; secretly he delivered his allegiance to Zhigao and also told Zhixun of Zhigao's secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: Tingwang was close to Zhigao's personal clerk Zhou Zong; he secretly offered his loyalty to Zhigao while also reporting Zhigao's intrigues back to Zhixun.

sentences.zh: 知詢召知誥詣金陵除父溫喪，知誥稱吳主之命不許，周宗謂廷望曰：「人言侍中有不臣七事，宜亟入謝！」

translations.literal: Zhixun summoned Zhigao to Jinling to observe mourning for his father Wen; Zhigao claimed the Wu ruler's order did not permit it; Zhou Zong told Tingwang: "People say the chief minister has seven acts of disloyalty—you should hurry in to apologize!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun summoned Zhigao to Jinling to mourn their father Wen, but Zhigao claimed the Wu ruler forbade it. Zhou Zong told Tingwang: "People say the chief minister has seven counts of disloyalty—you should hurry to Jiangdu and apologize!"

sentences.zh: 廷望還，以告知詢。

translations.literal: Tingwang returned and reported this to Zhixun.
translations.idiomatic: Tingwang returned and told Zhixun.

sentences.zh: 十一月，知詢入朝，知誥留知詢為統軍，領鎮海節度使，遣右雄武都指揮使柯厚征金陵兵還江都，知誥自是始專吳政。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Zhixun entered court; Zhigao retained Zhixun as overall commander, holding the Zhenhai military governorship; he dispatched right Intrepid Martial commanding commissioner Ke Hou to recall Jinling troops to Jiangdu; from this Zhigao first monopolized Wu governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhixun came to court; Zhigao kept him there as overall commander with the Zhenhai governorship, sent right Intrepid Martial commander Ke Hou to march Jinling's army back to Jiangdu, and from that point held Wu's government in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 知詢責知誥曰：「先王違世，兄為人子，初不臨喪，可乎？」

translations.literal: Zhixun reproached Zhigao: "When the former king departed the world, you as his son did not at first attend the mourning—is this permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun rebuked Zhigao: "When our father died, you as his son never came to mourn—is that acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 知誥曰：「爾挺劍待我，我何敢往！

translations.literal: Zhigao said: "You stood with drawn sword awaiting me—how could I dare go!
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao replied: "You waited for me with a drawn sword—how could I have gone!

sentences.zh: 爾為人臣，畜乘輿服御物，亦可乎！」

translations.literal: You are a subject of the state—yet you keep imperial carriage trappings and regalia—is that permissible!"
translations.idiomatic: You are a subject of the throne, yet you keep imperial carriage fittings and regalia—is that permissible!"

sentences.zh: 知詢又以廷望所言誥知誥，知誥曰：「以爾所為告我者，亦廷望也。」

translations.literal: Zhixun also told Zhigao what Tingwang had said; Zhigao said, "What you reported to me was also Tingwang's doing."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun repeated Tingwang's words to Zhigao. Zhigao replied, "The man who informed on you was Tingwang himself."

sentences.zh: 遂斬廷望。

translations.literal: He thereupon beheaded Tingwang.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Tingwang executed.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，吳主加尊號曰睿聖文明光孝皇帝，大赦，改元大和。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Wu ruler added the honorific title Sagely, Civilized, Luminous, and Filially Pious Emperor, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Dahe.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Wu emperor adopted the honorific Sagely, Civilized, Luminous, and Filially Pious Emperor, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Dahe.

sentences.zh: 康福行至方渠，羌胡出兵邀福，福擊走之；

translations.literal: Kang Fu traveled to Fangqu; Qiang and Hu tribes sent troops to intercept Fu; Fu struck and drove them off;
translations.idiomatic: Kang Fu reached Fangqu, where Qiang and Hu forces tried to intercept him; he routed them;

sentences.zh: 至青剛峽，遇吐蕃野利、大蟲二族數千帳，皆不覺唐兵至，福遣衛審𡷣掩擊，大破之，殺獲殆盡。

translations.literal: reaching Qinggang Gorge, he encountered several thousand tents of the Tibetan Yeli and Dachong tribes, all unaware Tang troops had arrived; Fu dispatched Wei Shenjuan to strike by surprise, greatly defeated them, and killed or captured nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinggang Gorge he came upon several thousand tents of the Tibetan Yeli and Dachong clans, none aware that Tang troops were near. He sent Wei Shenjuan in a surprise attack and shattered them, killing or capturing nearly everyone.

sentences.zh: 由是威聲大振，遂進至靈州，自是朔方始受代。

translations.literal: From this his martial renown greatly shook the region; he thereupon advanced to Lingzhou—from this time Shannan West began to accept replacement of commanders.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation soared, and he advanced to Lingzhou. From that point Shuofang began to accept regular turnover of its governors.

sentences.zh: 十二月，吳加徐知誥兼中書令，領寧國節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Wu added to Xu Zhigao the concurrent post of Palace Secretariat Director and command of Ningguo Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wu made Xu Zhigao concurrent palace secretariat director and military governor of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 知誥召徐知詢飲，以金鍾酌酒賜之，曰：「願弟壽千歲。」

translations.literal: Zhigao summoned Xu Zhixun to drink, poured wine with a golden bell and bestowed it on him, saying, "I wish my younger brother a thousand years of life."
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao invited Xu Zhixun to drink, poured wine from a golden bell, and offered it to him, saying, "May my younger brother live a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 知詢疑有毒，引他器均之，跽獻知誥曰：「願與兄各享五百歲。」

translations.literal: Zhixun suspected poison, drew another vessel to divide it evenly, knelt and presented it to Zhigao, saying, "I wish that you and I each enjoy five hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting poison, Zhixun poured the wine into another cup to split it evenly, knelt, and offered it back to Zhigao: "Then let us each enjoy five hundred years."

sentences.zh: 知誥變色，左右顧，不肯受，知詢捧酒不退。

translations.literal: Zhigao changed color; those beside him looked about; he would not accept it; Zhixun held the wine and would not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao's face darkened. His attendants glanced at one another; he refused the cup, but Zhixun would not lower it.

sentences.zh: 左右莫知所為，伶人申漸高徑前為詼諧語，掠二酒合飲之，懷金鐘趨出，知誥密遣人以良藥解之，已腦潰而卒。

translations.literal: Those beside them knew not what to do; actor Shen Jiangao stepped forward with jesting words, snatched both cups and drank them together, tucked the golden bell under his arm and hurried out; Zhigao secretly sent men with good medicine to save him, but his brain had already burst and he died.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew what to do until the actor Shen Jiangao stepped forward with a jest, seized both cups and drank them down together, tucked the golden bell under his arm, and hurried out. Zhigao secretly sent antidote, but Jiangao's brain had already ruptured and he died.

sentences.zh: 奉國節度使、知建州王延稟稱疾退居裡第，請以建州授其子繼雄；

translations.literal: Fengguo military governor and acting Jianzhou prefect Wang Yanbin claimed illness and retired to his private residence, requesting that Jianzhou be granted to his son Jixiong;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanbin, military governor of Fengguo and acting prefect of Jianzhou, claimed illness and retired home, asking that Jianzhou be given to his son Jixiong;

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔以繼雄為建州刺史。

translations.literal: on gengzi, an edict appointed Jixiong prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi an edict appointed Jixiong prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 安重誨既以李仁矩鎮閬州，使與綿州刺史武虔裕皆將兵赴治。

translations.literal: An Chonghui, having placed Li Renju in command at Langzhou, had him and Mianzhou prefect Wu Qianyu both lead troops to take up administration.
translations.idiomatic: After An Chonghui installed Li Renju at Langzhou, he ordered Renju and Wu Qianyu, prefect of Mianzhou, to bring troops and take up their posts.

sentences.zh: 虔裕，帝之故吏，重誨之外兄也。

translations.literal: Qianyu was an old retainer of the emperor and Chonghui's wife's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyu was an old retainer of the emperor and An Chonghui's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 重誨使仁矩詗董璋反狀，仁矩增飾而奏之。

translations.literal: Chonghui had Renju spy out Dong Zhang's rebellious conduct; Renju embellished it in his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui had Renju investigate Dong Zhang's disloyalty; Renju embellished the report before submitting it.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又使武信節度使夏魯奇治遂州城隍，繕甲兵，益兵戍之。

translations.literal: The court also had Wuxin military governor Xia Luqi repair Suizhou's walls and moat, ready arms and armor, and increase garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: The court also ordered Xia Luqi, military governor of Wuxin, to repair Suizhou's defenses, stock arms, and reinforce the garrison.

sentences.zh: 璋大懼。

translations.literal: Zhang was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was terrified.

sentences.zh: 時道路傳言，又將割綿、龍為節鎮，孟知祥亦懼。

translations.literal: At that time rumors along the roads said Mian and Long circuits would also be carved out as military commands; Meng Zhixiang was also afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Mian and Long would be carved into separate military commands, and Meng Zhixiang grew fearful as well.

sentences.zh: 璋素與知祥有隙，未嘗通問，至是，璋遣使詣成都，請為其子娶知祥女；

translations.literal: Zhang had long been at odds with Zhixiang and had never exchanged messages; at this time Zhang sent an envoy to Chengdu requesting his son marry Zhixiang's daughter;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Zhixiang had long been estranged and never exchanged messages. Now Zhang sent an envoy to Chengdu to ask that his son marry Zhixiang's daughter;

sentences.zh: 知祥許之，謀並力以拒朝廷。

translations.literal: Zhixiang agreed, plotting to join forces to resist the court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang agreed, and they plotted to join forces against the court.
